apps.name: gterm
apps.subtitle: iOS terminal app with SSH support, powered by the Ghostty engine (libghostty), with a custom on-screen keyboard
apps.localizedDescription:
gterm:

An iOS terminal app that renders with ghostty's libghostty engine (GPU/Metal, full xterm/VT emulation) and connects over SSH.

📲 Get the app: Download on the App Store (iOS 17+). Or sideload with AltStore or SideStore — both read the same source URL https://madeye.github.io/gterm/altstore.json.

iOS can't fork/exec a local shell, so gterm drives the terminal from an SSH connection via a custom passthru IO backend added to libghostty. See PLAN.md for the full architecture.

Status:

• ✅ libghostty passthru IO backend (madeye/ghostty).
• ✅ iOS app; ghostty terminal surface renders on device/simulator.
• ✅ Lean Swift layer over libghostty (app, surface view, input).
• ✅ SSH transport (swift-nio-ssh): password auth, PTY shell, window-change.
• ✅ Custom on-screen keyboard (esc/ctrl/alt/tab/arrows/symbols, sticky mods).
• ✅ Saved connections (Keychain passwords) + trust-on-first-use host keys.

apps.name: PaperPad
apps.subtitle: Paper Mario 64, native for Mac, iOS, and iPadOS
apps.localizedDescription:
PaperPad:

PaperPad combines the pmret Paper Mario decompilation with the statically recompiled runtime and renderer maintained by Paper-Mario-ReCut. It adds a native Apple application shell, Metal presentation, keyboard and controller input, customizable touch controls, native settings, and private first-run ROM import.

PaperPad is a game-specific static recompile, not a general Nintendo 64 emulator. It currently supports only an unmodified Paper Mario (US) 1.0 ROM supplied by the user.

This repository contains integration source, patches, scripts, and documentation. It does not contain Paper Mario, a ROM, extracted Nintendo assets, generated playable game code, saves, or a playable ROM-derived archive. Read the rights and licensing boundary before redistributing source or a build.

apps.name: Solstice
apps.subtitle: Mobile variant of Horizon
apps.localizedDescription: Mobile variant of Horizon.

versions.localizedDescription:
Built on Horizon 2.3.3.

This release rounds out the new mobile notifications on both Android and iOS and fixes the cramped log viewer.

Changes since v2026.6.3:

• Richer message notifications. Incoming messages now vibrate correctly, show an unread count, and collapse into one notification per conversation instead of stacking up.
• Message notifications are tagged as messages on Android (#14). They now use the system's message category, so they behave correctly with Do Not Disturb allow-lists, notification history, and paired watches.
• Notifications respect the ring switch on Android (#13). With your phone set to vibrate or silent, an incoming message vibrates instead of pinging out loud. (iOS already honored the silent switch.).
• Steadier background connection on iOS. The audio keep-alive now recovers after the system resets its media server, so the app is less likely to go quiet while backgrounded.
• The log viewer fills the screen (#12). The conversation log list now uses the full height of the window instead of being squeezed into a sliver beneath the filters, and it shrinks correctly when the keyboard opens.

Built on Horizon 2.3.3.

This brings Solstice up to date with three Horizon releases (2.3.1, 2.3.2, and 2.3.3) worth of fixes and improvements since 2026.6.2.

Changes since v2026.6.2:

• Log viewer search now highlights matches. Filtering for a word in the log viewer, or using find while reading a conversation, highlights it in the results.
• Backup imports work on a fresh install again. Importing a manual backup into a completely empty log folder no longer leaves the imported logs broken.
• Fewer friends-list glitches. Friends and bookmarks no longer show up twice in some cases.
• Stuck link previews and cut-off BBCode fixed. URL previews no longer sometimes stay open, and BBCode is no longer cut off in the profile viewer's Recent Messages block or in character hover previews.

• Grouped pins and memos cleanup. Deleted or banned channels no longer stay stuck in your grouped pins throwing errors on every connect, and saved character memos no longer come back with garbled text.

See the Horizon changelog for the full upstream detail.

Built on Horizon 2.2.1.

A stability release: I think I've finally fixed the root cause of the app freezing, not just the symptoms.

apps.name: Pocket8
apps.subtitle: An iOS Native Emulator for the PICO-8 fantasy console. Free and Open Source. Experimental Alpha available for Android!
apps.localizedDescription:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec24f92e-d29a-4319-8293-439487d60b35

Features:

• Native Engine: Runs flawlessly on iOS, due to the official PICO-8 engine being implemented as a WASM module.
• Quick Save & Load: The only PICO-8 experience with instant save states. Freeze time and resume anywhere, across devices.

• Adaptive Controls: Custom Gameboy-esque controls with tactile haptics. Works in portrait and landscape. Swap to virtual joystick.

• Smart Library: Automatically extracts cartridge labels and metadata, presenting your collection in a polished grid.

Technical Look:

The core engineering challenge was reconciling the asynchronous nature of mobile file I/O with the synchronous requirements of the Emscripten/WASM virtual file system.

PICO-8 demands a synchronous file system. Bridging this to mobile required completely reverse-engineering the Emscripten boot sequence.

apps.name: Blinker Fluid
apps.subtitle: Chromium Blink + V8 browser engine ported to iOS 15.4 with no WebKit
apps.localizedDescription:
About:

Blinker Fluid is an experimental privacy-focused browser that ports Chromium's Blink rendering engine and V8 JavaScript engine to iOS, allowing websites to run without relying on Apple's built-in WebKit engine.

The project primarily targets jailbroken and TrollStore-capable devices, bringing a Chromium-based browser to older iOS versions where the bundled version of WebKit may struggle with some modern websites.

Why?:

I started Blinker Fluid because Ungoogled Chromium is my primary desktop browser (not counting Tor), and I wanted to see if Chromium's Blink engine could run on jailbroken iOS.

Another reason was that many modern websites no longer work correctly with older versions of WebKit bundled with older iOS releases, which many jailbroken users are unable or unwilling to update from.

apps.localizedDescription:
Absorb:

A modern audiobookshelf client with a card-based player experience.

A note on AI: Absorb is developed by a human with AI assistance (mostly Claude Code) helping write, refactor, and review code. It's not "vibe coded" or auto-generated, every change is reviewed, tested, and shipped intentionally. That said, I'm all in on AI as a development tool. It massively speeds up the work and lets a solo developer ship features and fixes at a pace that wouldn't be possible otherwise. I'm sharing this openly so you know what's behind the app.

Features:

• Card-based player — full-screen "Absorbing" cards replace the traditional player screen.
• Audiobookshelf integration — connects to your self-hosted audiobookshelf server.

• Podcast support — chaptered podcasts with rich HTML descriptions.

apps.name: HarkinianPad

apps.localizedDescription:
HarkinianPad:

HarkinianPad packages the full Ship of Harkinian source port as a native iOS/iPadOS app. It renders through Metal, imports a user-provided supported Ocarina of Time ROM through Files, and includes a landscape touch controller that can be hidden whenever a physical controller is connected.

This repository contains the mobile integration and reproducible build scripts. It does not contain Ocarina of Time, a ROM, or a playable ROM-derived archive. See the scoped rights and licensing boundary; it does not relicense Shipwright, third-party projects, or game material.

Install status:

The current development build has been signed, installed, and played on a 12.9-inch iPad Pro (6th generation) running iPadOS 26.5.2. Files import, on-device archive loading, touch gameplay, save loading, the settings menu, and in-place app updates have all been exercised on that hardware.

What changed:

HarkinianPad does not include a ROM or extracted Ocarina of Time game data. You must supply legally obtained game data yourself.

SHA-256:

bc1f4f8a8306fa0ef1ebd3ad47005f73b1d49e4ca671d6084f23fbc56ad0293d.

Validation:

• Built from a clean checkout with Xcode 26.6 against the iOS 26.5 SDK for arm64; minimum iOS version is 14.0.
• GitHub repository-safety and full unsigned iPhoneOS build checks passed before merge.
• The exact tagged IPA payload was re-signed locally with an Apple Development identity and update-installed without deleting the app on a physical iPhone 14 and iPad Pro.
• Both devices report HarkinianPad version 0.1.0 (3); the iPad launched successfully and remained live.
• Existing phone and tablet touch-layout preferences remained byte-for-byte identical across both in-place updates.

• The public IPA contains no ROM, user-generated oot*.o2r archive, signing profile, or code signature. Its bundled soh.o2r is the ROM-free Shipwright port-resource archive.

• The exact-payload launch request on the iPhone was blocked because the device was locked; its installation, version, signature, and preserved preferences were verified.

• The full lifecycle and audio-route interruption matrix remains incomplete.

apps.name: F0X
apps.subtitle: Native F-Zero X source port via G-Diffuser for Apple Silicon macOS, iPhone, and iPad, with Metal and touch controls
apps.localizedDescription:
F0X:

Evidence.

F0X packages the native decompiled F-Zero X game logic from G-Diffuser with libultraship/Fast3D and its Metal backend. It is a source-port integration, not a general Nintendo 64 emulator.

This repository contains the Apple integration, maintained patches, documentation, and original F0X artwork. It does not contain F-Zero X, a ROM, extracted Nintendo assets, saves, or a playable ROM-derived archive. You must supply your own legally acquired supported cartridge dump; setup and extraction happen locally, and nothing is uploaded.

versions.localizedDescription:
Developer Preview 2 repairs controller sleep, disconnect, and reconnect handling in the libultraship ControlDeck SDL2 backend. Stale handles are reconciled against current devices at events, foreground resume, and a bounded active check; surviving player slots remain stable and held input is neutralized on disconnect.

The attached IPA is ROM-free, unsigned, arm64, and targets iOS/iPadOS 16 or newer. It must be re-signed with your own Apple identity. Install it over the existing com.chrissotraidis.f0x app to preserve local data; do not uninstall first.

Automated virtual-controller coverage passed 42/42. Physical iPad in-place install, gameplay boot, foreground resume, and data preservation passed. Hands-on Bluetooth, wired, natural-sleep, full-mapping, and multi-controller acceptance remain open.

F0X 0.1.0 Developer Preview 1:

The first downloadable F0X developer preview for iPhone and iPad.

Before installing:

• This IPA is unsigned. Re-sign it with your own Apple identity using Xcode or a compatible personal-signing method.
• It requires an arm64 iPhone or iPad running iOS/iPadOS 16 or newer.
• F-Zero X is not included. On first launch, choose your own legally acquired supported US revision 0 ROM from Files; extraction stays local.
• To preserve saves, settings, and touch layouts during an update, install over the existing com.chrissotraidis.f0x app. Do not uninstall first.

Highlights:

• Native Apple Silicon game logic with Metal rendering.
• Independent, customizable iPhone and iPad touch layouts.
• One-second racing-only A acceleration latch.
• Corrected cartridge audio synthesis and menu timing.
• Corrected course-preview scaling.
• Repaired repeated back/forward GP menu navigation.
• Local ROM validation and on-device extraction.
• Keyboard and compatible physical-controller support.

Validation:

• Physical iPad: owner-accepted normal game start, touch racing, audio, and course presentation.
• Physical iPhone 14: latest build installed and running with ROM, archive, save, configuration, and accepted touch profile preserved byte-for-byte.
• Deterministic repeated menu-navigation regression reaches GP Race.
• Touch merge/profile suite: 87/87.
• IPA ZIP integrity: 85 entries, no errors.
• ROM/save/signing audit: clean.

Hands-on iPhone gameplay, alternate audio routes, interruptions, controllers, stress multi-touch, thermals, and long sessions remain broader preview testing areas.

apps.localizedDescription:
MaskPad:

MaskPad packages the full 2 Ship 2 Harkinian source port as a native landscape iOS/iPadOS app. It renders through Metal, imports a user-provided supported Majora's Mask ROM through Files, and adds a phone/tablet touch controller with movable, resizable, and hideable controls.

This repository contains the mobile integration and reproducible build scripts. It does not contain Majora's Mask, a ROM, or a playable ROM-derived archive. See the scoped rights and licensing boundary; it does not relicense third-party projects or game material.

versions.localizedDescription:
MaskPad v0.1.2:

This release repairs SDL2 controller sleep, disconnect, and reconnect handling in libultraship's existing controller manager.

• closes stale or disconnected controller handles instead of leaving them in a player slot.
• preserves valid player ownership and returns a sole reconnecting controller to player 1.
• assigns genuinely additional controllers to the next free slot.

• reconciles at startup, controller events, foreground resume, and a bounded active check.
• adds deterministic missed-removal, held-input, player-slot, remap, and foreground regression coverage.

The attached IPA is ROM-free and unsigned. It contains no provisioning profile or maintainer signing identity and must be signed with your own Apple account before installation. Supply your own legally acquired supported game data after installation.

Version: 0.1.2 Build: 3.

Physical Bluetooth, wired, natural-sleep, full-mapping, rumble/motion, and two-controller acceptance remain device-specific hands-on gates; automated controller reconciliation and hosted build/UI checks passed.

Kavi (Flashcards):

Kavi is a native, local-first iOS study and flashcards app built for fast card creation, focused revision, and full ownership of your data.

apps.name: Manic EMU
apps.subtitle: Manic EMU is an all-in-one retro game emulator for iOS. It packs powerful features while keeping a clean, sleek UI and delivering buttery-smooth gameplay
apps.localizedDescription:
Manic EMU is an all-in-one retro game emulator for iOS. It brings console, arcade, computer, and mobile Java systems into one app while keeping a clean, sleek UI and smooth gameplay-focused controls.

The sections below keep the app details up front, then connect availability, features, development notes, related documentation, repository layout, and licensing in one place.

Manic EMU does not include ROMs, ISOs, BIOS files, or copyrighted game data. Use legally owned backups, homebrew, and public-domain software only. See the upstream anti-piracy policy for the full project position.

At a Glance:

• App distribution: App Store, StikStore, and SideStore.
• Source target: iOS app built with Xcode 16+, iOS SDK 15+, and Swift 5.9+.
• Emulator model: multiple emulator cores, including Libretro-based frameworks and dedicated cores.

versions.localizedDescription:
Starting from version 2.0.0, we no longer provide builds of TrollStore JIT. You can package it yourself by following the guide.

This is a major release focused on a redesigned interface, expanded platform support, and advanced features. Landscape browsing, library management, and external controller navigation have been rebuilt. It also adds several new systems and brings Netplay to eligible Libretro cores.

Before You Update:

• Dreamcast (Flycast): Existing save states will no longer work as of 2.0.0. Convert important save states to in-game saves before updating, or back up the Flycast/dc folder yourself.
• Wii: A BootMii-format keys.bin is required.
• Symbian: Install firmware in Settings first (.ROM; S60v2 and later also need .RPKG).
• GameCube / Wii: The core is still being optimized, so heat and frame drops should still be expected.
• MAME: A number of lesser-used arcade systems have been trimmed. Some obscure titles may no longer run.

Interface:

Landscape.

• A new landscape library, with most landscape pages redesigned.
• Built-in dynamic backgrounds. You can use or upload ShaderToy (GLSL) scripts to customize them. Only single-Image scripts are supported; complex scripts may increase battery use or heat.
• Multiple customizable card carousel styles.
• Focused background: when a game is selected, its banner can be used as the landscape focus backdrop.
• background music feature in landscape mode—besides built-in tracks, you can upload your own music files to use as background music.
• built in 12 sets of navigation and focus sound effects.

Game Options and Shortcuts.

• A unified options list and interaction model throughout the app.
• Available actions are automatically arranged and regrouped for the current context.
• Advanced reordering: customize the order and grouping of options.
• A redesigned in-game shortcut menu. Shortcuts can appear on supported skins and in the in-game menu.

Navigation and Input.

• A global focus and navigation system for iPhone and iPad. You can browse and interact entirely with a controller or keyboard.
• Hold Command or the controller’s Select button to view the shortcut cheatsheet.
• A unified navigation bar for more consistent browsing and editing.
• Many long-press and hidden actions have been replaced with more conventional, iOS-style interactions.
• Batch management and actions.
• Adaptive rotation throughout the app.
• Controllers can be assigned to a player slot. On cores that expect a keyboard, controller inputs can be mapped to keyboard events.

Features:

Library and Artwork.

• Covers now support separate icon and banner artwork. Box art is used in regular lists, icons in square layouts, and banners as the landscape focus backdrop.
• Online artwork from Libretro Thumbnails and SteamGridDB (Grids / Heroes / Logos / Icons; SteamGridDB requires your own API key).
• Switching platform or category rematches cover art.

Game Data.

• ESRB ratings and matching icons. Rating icons can be hidden in Settings.
• A redesigned save-state manager with import and export.
• Scoped settings: the same option can be stored at game, platform, or global level, and each can be cleared or reset independently.
• batch scraping for covers, icons, and banners.

Shaders and Skins.

• Real-time shader preview, without loading the shader first.
• Redesigned default GBA skin.
• Flex skins now support customizing button size and position.

Achievements, Cheats, and Netplay.

• RetroAchievements pages are easier to read and load faster.
• MultiSet support: earn subset achievements without a patched ROM. Switching the achievement list only changes what is shown; it does not affect which sets you can unlock while playing.
• Online cheat database: search, multi-select add, and bookmarks.
• Netplay for many Libretro cores: host or join a room, public lobby, LAN scan, relay, spectator mode, and room password. Your Adventurer Card nickname is used as the Netplay display name. You can now trade treasured Pokémon with friends over the network, or go head-to-head on arcade systems.
• Rewind: add it to the shortcut menu, a controller mapping, or TriggerPro, then touch and hold to use it.

Advanced Features and Import.

• Core Settings: intended for advanced users. Incorrect values may prevent games from launching. Settings can be reset per game or per platform.
• Settings now include an Adventurer Card, with a customizable nickname and avatar.
• Import games from DukeX.
• Import games from Armsx2.
• PS1 now supports importing .bin files directly.

New Systems and Cores:

Symbian (EKA2L1).

• Supports S60v1, N-Gage 1.0, S60v2, S60v3, N-Gage 2.0, S60v5, and Symbian^3.
• Touch input, firmware management, and system apps.
• Legacy / PPL / TXM JIT.

PC Engine (Beetle PCE).

• Supports TurboGrafx-16, TurboGrafx-CD, and SuperGrafx, with subcategory switching.

Neo Geo Pocket / Color (Beetle NeoPop).

• Supports Neo Geo Pocket and Neo Geo Pocket Color, with subcategory switching.

Commodore 64 (VICE x64sc).

• Full keyboard support, with switching between gamepad and keyboard skins.

Amiga (PUAE).

• Full keyboard support, with switching between gamepad and keyboard skins.

GameCube / Wii (Dolphin).

• Legacy / PPL / TXM JIT.
• Wii: Wiimote sideways mode.
• Dolphin cheats, including Action Replay Max decryption.
• Wiimote skins for Wii.

Other Cores.

• Mesen-S added for SNES / GB / GBC.
• gpSP added for GBA, and can be switched with mGBA and VBA-M.

JIT Fixes and Improvements:

• Fixed JIT failing on TXM devices running iOS 26.6 and later.
• Revised TXM device detection.
• N64 GLideN64 and ParaLLEl RDP now both support JIT.

Core Updates:

The following cores have been updated to the latest upstream stable releases.

• 3DS (Azahar, Citra).
• PS1 (Beetle PSX HW).
• DOS (DOSBox Pure).
• Dreamcast (Flycast) — see the save-state migration note above.
• NDS (melonDS).
• PSP (PPSSPP).
• N64 (Mupen64Plus).

Fixes:

• Numerous bug fixes and performance optimizations.

Urgent fix for J2ME (J2meJS) save file loading error Fixed the issue where Artic Base couldn't select the Australia region 3DS (Azahar) adds HLE and LLE emulation accuracy options. Fixed NDS crash when using Flex Skin.

Heads up: v1.9.1 will corrupt save files in J2ME (J2meJS core), and we’re really sorry about that. As a temporary workaround, we suggest backing up the save file "XXX.j2mejs.srm" in the "Manic EMU - Datas" folder. We'll look into whether we can recover the save data.

JIT (iOS 26 & Earlier):

• Implemented broad JIT support compatible with iOS 26 and earlier versions.
• Integrated support for StikDebug’s universal.js launcher (Special thanks to @Stossy11).
• Added JIT support for:.

• 3DS (Citra).
• Dreamcast (Flycast).
• Nintendo DS (melonDS).
• Nintendo 64 (GLideN64 RDP / mupen64plus.next Special thanks to @Fareblyat).
• DOS (dosbox-pure).
• PlayStation 1 (beetle-psx).
• Added setting to enable/re-enable JIT directly from the app.
• Improved JIT handling flow for iOS 26 (automatic redirect to reinitialize when required).

Core & Emulator Updates:

• Updated 3DS (Azahar) to latest upstream.
• Updated PSP (PPSSPP) to latest upstream.
• Added SNES core (snes9x; sideloaded availability).
• Added PS1 core (PCSX-ReARMed).

3DS Improvements:

• Fixed Vulkan-related crashes (Azahar).

• Added Artic Base Home Menu support.
• Added support for transferring data from real hardware via Artic Base.
• Added Pretendo network configuration support.
• Improved Home Menu integration (direct install logic).
• Added fast-forward support (Citra).
• Added full-screen AirPlay mirroring (Citra).

PSP:

• Added support for installing homebrew via ZIP import.

DOS:

• Added thumbstick to default DOS skin.

J2ME:

• Performance optimizations (J2meJS).

Controls & Input:

• Added support for direct native keyboard event mapping.

• TriggerPro now supports native keyboard event mapping.

UI & Customization:

• Added new app icons.
• Added default emulator core selection setting.
• Added “Hide Platform” feature.
• Added manufacturer-based sorting.

• Improved theme customization options.

Library / Platform Organization:

• Game Boy can now be categorized as Chromatic (CHM).
• DOS can now be categorized under Windows 95 / Windows 98.

apps.name: MiruShin
apps.subtitle: Your anime, movies, and shows: discover, track, and watch in one beautiful app
apps.localizedDescription:
What You Can Do:

More goodies.

• 📺 Android TV with remote-friendly navigation throughout.
• 🖼️ Picture-in-Picture and native player handoff where the platform supports it.
• 🔐 Host-controlled watch-party permissions for guest play/pause, seek, and speed changes.

• 🔄 Tracker sync for AniList, MyAnimeList, and Shikimori account workflows.
• 📤 Exports to MyAnimeList XML and Shikimori JSON.
• 🧩 Add-ons (Sora-compatible modules) for source search, installable by URL.

Download:

Windows: the .exe installer is unsigned, so Microsoft Defender may show a false-positive warning. If that happens, use the .msi installer or the portable .zip instead.

versions.localizedDescription:
MiruShin continues to evolve as a modern and comfortable way to watch and discover media, with each update focused on making the experience smoother, cleaner, and more enjoyable across the app.

What's New:

• Fixed missing next-episode countdowns when AniList libraries are merged with MAL fallback data.

v2.8.7:

• Improved Watch Order with theme-colored current-title highlighting, personal score, and favorite status.

v2.8.6:

• Fixed player sessions not terminating correctly and restored proper playback speed handling.
• Fixed expired airing schedules still appearing in the Library.
• Improved seeking controls by separating arrow tap and hold behavior.

v2.8.5:

• Fixed streams freezing during startup and playback unexpectedly resuming after being paused.
• Fixed playback-speed changes causing stalls or showing a speed that was not actually applied.

• Added accumulated seek-distance feedback when repeatedly using the left and right arrow keys.
• Improved the Library AniList outage notice with scrolling, MyAnimeList fallback status, dismissal, and correct spacing.

v2.8.2:

• Improved add-on import, export, and backup reliability across devices.
• Fixed add-on restoration so exported configurations retain required module data and settings.

v2.8.1:

• Fixed MAL and Shikimori fallback responses overriding AniList library status and progress after an AniList outage.
• AniList now remains canonical when selected as the primary tracker, while fallback snapshots stay available without reopening completed titles.
• Local changes made during an outage remain queued and sync to AniList first, then independently to connected MyAnimeList and Shikimori accounts.
• Prevented automatic playback progress from reopening completed titles or dropping rewatching status.
• Entry edits now sync only fields that actually changed, so score or notes edits cannot overwrite status or progress.

v2.8.0:

• Added MyAnimeList fallback for AniList outages across Board, Discovery, media details, Library, and Watch Order, with automatic return to AniList after recovery.
• Added local-first tracking: progress, favorites, status, score, notes, repeat count, and dates are saved locally and safely synchronized later.
• AniList, MAL, and Shikimori now synchronize independently using stable media identity, offline mutation queues, provider health tracking, and conflict resolution.
• Library filters, sorting, Watch, Edit, Play, and continue-watching now work with locally cached and MAL fallback data during AniList outages.
• Fixed AniList outage banner spacing in Library to match Board and Discovery.

• Video quality can differ between participants while the episode, module, server, and voiceover remain synchronized.

• Added a dedicated Buy Me a Coffee support card after Accounts in AniList Settings and below MiruShin updates in TMDB Settings.

v2.7.12:

• Fixed Security Check verification loops on macOS and iOS.
• Fixed content not loading after completing verification.
• Prevented duplicate Security Check windows from opening.
• Improved cookie persistence and browser session handling during verification.
• Fixed offline HLS playback on macOS.

v2.7.11:

• Improved AniList reliability with a 30-second timeout and one automatic retry before falling back to cached data.

v2.7.10:

• Added automatic anime Watch Order with full franchise discovery and a Main story only filter.
• Added AniList progress and bold, theme-colored status labels to Watch Order.
• Replaced Related Titles with a cleaner, transparent Watch Order list.
• Cached Anime Themes for the current session to prevent repeated loading.

v2.7.9:

• Added clean share links for AniList anime and manga and TMDB movies and TV shows.
• Improved link safety while keeping existing MiruShin links fully compatible.

v2.7.8:

• Added clearly labeled IMDb ratings to TMDB movie/series and matched AniList anime detail pages, displayed directly after the original score.
• Profile action cards now fit up to five per row on larger screens, with additional cards wrapping cleanly.

v2.7.7:

• Fixed Compact Cards appearing outside the row edges while scrolling, while preserving hover effects.
• Compact Cards are now disabled by default; existing saved preferences remain unchanged.

v2.7.6:

• Expanded the AniList Board with Favorites, Airing, Upcoming, Finished, Newest, and Recently Updated sections.
• Added adaptive pagination to Board and Discovery: compact rows load automatically, while wide grids offer Load More and fetch results based on screen size.
• Made compact cards the default and improved responsive layouts with up to eight columns.
• Polished poster clipping, gradients, hover animations, and button press effects.
• Reduced the media-details hero height and improved Board loading feedback.

v2.7.5:

• Added a Fanart.tv-powered Gallery to Media Details with 4K-first backgrounds, cached results, and an optional securely stored API key in Settings.
• Added a fullscreen Gallery viewer with original-resolution artwork, swipe and arrow navigation, zooming, and an image counter.

• Improved Discovery on large screens with responsive filter controls and up to eight poster columns while preserving compact mobile layouts.

v2.7.4:

• Added cross-platform MiruShin deep links for opening AniList and TMDB titles directly in the app.

• Opening an AniList or TMDB MiruShin link now automatically switches to the matching catalog.
• Watch with Friends default invites now use normal clickable HTTPS links, while existing mirushin:// invite links remain supported.
• Improved Self-hosted Relay invites with cleaner direct HTTPS links and browser landing pages for opening rooms in MiruShin.
• Added a Setup Guide button for Self-hosted Relay configuration, with English, Russian, and Japanese localization.
• Improved macOS fullscreen transitions so the player waits for the native fullscreen transition to actually finish before closing or opening the next episode.
• Improved timeline hover and drag handling, preventing seek previews and player controls from getting stuck after fullscreen or window-state changes.
• Improved progressive seek previews to prefer the later thumbnail when two cached frames are equally close to the selected position.
• Fixed backup exports not correctly including some saved list-based settings and filters on desktop platforms.

v2.7.3:

• Added cross-platform MiruShin deep links for opening AniList and TMDB titles directly in the app on Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, and iOS.
• Added shareable MiruShin links to media details, alongside the original AniList or TMDB page links.

• Opening an AniList or TMDB MiruShin link now automatically switches to the matching catalog.
• Watch with Friends default invites now use a normal clickable HTTPS link that opens the room in MiruShin, while existing mirushin:// invites remain supported.
• Improved Self-hosted Relay invites with clean HTTPS links using the relay address directly, without redundant relay or transport parameters.
• Added browser landing pages for Self-hosted Relay invites with an Open in MiruShin action.

v2.7.2:

• Sync your status, episode progress, and score across AniList, MyAnimeList, and Shikimori.
• Sign in securely from Settings -> Connections using OAuth.
• Choose your Library source from AniList, MyAnimeList, or Shikimori.
• Offline updates are now queued and synced automatically when you are back online.
• Added optional custom API credentials for MyAnimeList and Shikimori.

v1.8.1:

• Fixed auto next episode and watched progress triggering too early on unstable or reloaded streams.
• Next episode button now counts down 5 to 1, then closes the player if you don't continue.
• Next episode button shows shortly after the episode ends instead of instantly.
• Added a keyboard shortcuts and touch gestures panel in player settings.
• New keys: C toggles subtitles, P enters Picture in Picture, V skips intro/outro or goes to next episode.

v1.8.0:

• Added an Episodes button in the player so you can jump to any episode directly.
• Improved player controls so labels switch to icons earlier and never feel cramped.

• Now Playing now shows the real AniList/TMDB title in your selected language, with smart fallback support.
• Fixed TMDB library progress showing 0% instead of the correct watch percentage.
• Settings now adapt to your selected catalog mode.
• TMDB mode now hides AniList options and accounts.
• AniList mode now hides TMDB-specific options.
• Removed the redundant TMDB enable toggle.
• Added a new Compact cards toggle for Board cards.

• Removed unused settings: Poster card style, Subtitle preferred language, and Region/country.
• Removed the redundant Discovery status bar for a cleaner browsing experience.

v1.7.3:

• Fixed Android TV D-pad navigation on the Home and Discovery screens: focus no longer skips the movie posters and jumps straight to the "see more" / "Load more" button, so you can now reach and select every poster.

v1.7.2:

• Fixed playback speed not being restored after the player restarts.
• Added a short delay before auto-playing the next episode after the current stream finishes.

v1.7.1:

• Added Clear All and Apply buttons to the source filter.
• Updated several localization strings.

v1.7.0:

• Added a new Sources page. You can open it from the Sources button on the Addons page.

• You can open a source, browse its addons, and install them into your library with one tap.
• Addons that are already installed are now clearly marked.
• Added search by addon name, author, language, and type.
• Added filters for multiple languages and types at the same time, for example Russian + English or anime + movies.

• You can now refresh, rename, copy the URL, or remove a source.
• Removing a source will not remove your installed addons.

v1.6.4:

• Added support for adding addons by addon ID.

v1.6.3:

• Fixed watch progress not tracking for TMDB episodes in the local library, including across auto-next season changes.

v1.6.2:

• Fixed auto-next episode and watch progress for auto-played episodes.

• Previously, when an episode started automatically, watch progress was not saved and the next episode did not play correctly.
• Now every episode saves progress, marks itself as watched at 85%, and reliably continues to the next episode.

v1.6.0:

• Android TV support with Leanback launcher/banner, TV-aware navigation, focus rings, and d-pad-friendly cards.
• Player remote fixes: OK play/pause, paused UI focus navigation, Settings/Quality/Episodes/Subtitles reachable by d-pad, sliders no longer trap focus, Back hides chrome first.
• Android TV WebView cursor improvements: smaller/smoother cursor, native tap fallback, better keyboard/textbox handling, and cursor support for YouTube trailers.
• AniList editor improvements from TV: hold OK on media cards opens entry edit actions where supported.
• Library/search/addon/settings text fields improved for d-pad escape.
• Playback fixes including seek/d-pad fixes, PiP handling fixes, iOS PiP fix, and player back-button fixes.
• AniList and Shikimori metadata/library fixes.

v1.5.0:

• Improved auto-next episode, mark as watched, and AniList sync.
• Fixed progress on finished streams, even when the stream jumps back to 0:00.
• Fixed player controls and mouse cursor not hiding after auto-next.
• Fixed buffering spinner sometimes staying visible after playback resumes.
• AniList now marks anime as Completed when you finish the last known episode.
• Fixed Trailer button, now it appears correctly on all devices.
• Moved Auto AniList progress setting, now it only shows in the AniList catalog.
• Fixed settings not saving after app restart.
• Poster card style and compact mode are now remembered.

v1.4.4:

• TMDB metadata now loads on first launch without setup.
• Added a Use custom API key option in Settings -> API Connections.
• You can still use your own TMDB Read Access Token if needed.

v1.4.3:

• The player now automatically tries another playback method when needed.

v1.4.2:

v1.4.1:

• Fixed WebView support on Windows. YouTube trailers now play correctly on Windows.

v1.4.0:

v1.3.8:

v1.3.6:

v1.3.5:

• Fixed slow Choose Episode loading for custom/addon sources.
• Episodes from the addon now appear first, using the addon’s own episode name and poster when available.

v1.3.4:

v1.3.3:

apps.name: Edge
apps.subtitle: App which allows you to use your health devices beyond subscriptions. Supports Workout Tracking, Nutrition Tracking, Wellness Excercise, Sleep, Recovery, Strain, and Many more
apps.localizedDescription:
Openstrap Edge:

An app that makes your wearable useful without its subscription. Pairs over Bluetooth, computes everything on your phone, iOS and Android. WHOOP 4/5/MG get full support today; see Supports for what else it talks to.

Not affiliated with WHOOP. Not a clone of their app or their scores — see below.

As featured in:

"The goal of the so-called OpenStrap project is not to re-create the WHOOP app. Rather, the algorithms and processing methods are developed from scratch, based on public research… The health data collected from the watch never leaves the phone.".

— Hackaday, 15 July 2026.

versions.localizedDescription:
This release adds support for additional heart-rate devices, introduces several new tracking options, and includes a number of accuracy, reliability, and data-quality fixes.

New Device Support:

• Added support for Bluetooth heart-rate chest straps for basic heart-rate tracking.
• Added support for Oura Ring for basic heart-rate tracking.
• Added Spanish, French, German, Chinese, and Hindi translations. The language can be changed from Profile.
• Chest strap and Oura support currently provides heart-rate data only. These devices do not provide the full range of analytics available with WHOOP data.

New Features:

• Added daily step goals. Goals can be set and edited from the app.
• Added workout detection prompts for workouts that have been left running. The app will ask whether you are still working out instead of continuing to record indefinitely.
• Added Bowling as a workout type.
• Added a General/Custom workout type for activities that are not covered by the existing list.
• Added the ability to mark a recorded night as "Not sleep".
• Restored the "Track something else" free-text journal entry.

Recovery:

Fixed an issue where Recovery could remain permanently stuck at "Not scored". Certain data-cleanup operations could remove the baseline used to calculate Recovery, leaving the score unable to recover.

The common case is now handled correctly. One edge case remains: nights where no sleep is detected at all.

Sleep:

Fixed an issue where short periods of sleep around midnight could be assigned to both adjacent nights. This could result in inflated sleep-need calculations on both days.

Sleep data exported to Apple Health has also been rewritten to export as a continuous night instead of multiple fragmented sleep periods.

Heart Rate:

Fixed an issue where Zone 5 could be reached too easily before the app had observed a user's actual maximum heart rate. The previous fallback maximum could result in excessive effort being attributed to the highest zone.

Improved irregular heart rhythm detection so that a single irregular reading no longer triggers an alert. Alerts now require a sustained irregular pattern.

Fixed several cases where daily calorie totals could be inaccurate:

• Walking calories were not always calculated using the user's actual pace.
• Calories from a workout that ended early could be lost.
• Cancelled workouts could leave calories incorrectly included in the daily total.

WHOOP:

Fixed wake alarms on some WHOOP 4 devices that failed to trigger because the app was sending a command format that the firmware did not execute.

Added support for pairing WHOOP 5 and WHOOP MG.

Language:

Fixed an issue where the app could default to German on first launch regardless of the device's configured language.

Also corrected a number of French and German translation issues, including grammar and pluralization.

Backups:

Improved handling of corrupted NOOP backup files. The app now clearly reports when a backup is damaged instead of silently failing or presenting a misleading error.

Reliability:

Included additional fixes for device synchronization, connection stability, and general reliability.

Known Limitations:

• Bluetooth heart-rate chest straps and Oura currently provide heart-rate data only and do not receive the full analytics available from WHOOP data.
• A genuinely corrupted NOOP backup cannot currently be recovered. The import process can identify and report the corruption, but data that is already damaged in the source file cannot be restored.
• The remaining Recovery edge case involving nights with no detected sleep is still being tracked separately.

• fix(ble): arm gen4 wake alarm with the rev-1 9-byte form the firmware executes.
• fix(derive): cap the live-workout derive hold so a forgotten session cannot blank Home.
• feat(ble): close the gen5/MG pairing gap (no wire-format in edge).
• feat(workout): "Still working out?" nudge for a forgotten live session.
• fix(sync): enforce safe Gen5 history task boundaries.
• feat(energy): price walking into Active energy from measured cadence (v77).
• band-agnostic: storage, ble seam, and the first non-whoop device.
• fix irregular rhythm notification firing almost every day.
• fix ios build: known out of scope in AccessorySetup.
• language picker in profile.
• add es/fr/de/zh/hi translations.
• fix: activity-type edit regression + Active Energy workout-gap credit.
• i18n: migrate onboarding + profile strings.
• urgent: fix app defaulting to german on fresh install.
• fix(ble): the official gen5 connection bootstrap, through READY.
• fix(zones): anchor zone edges on max(observed ceiling, age estimate).
• fix gen5 pairing test pinning a stale present signature.
• gate the workout health write on a delete that actually cleared.
• i18n: finish the sweep across lib/ui2 + shared band/source components.
• add bowling and a general workout, and title Health Connect records.
• step goal editing + dashed calibrating rings.
• fix a batch of small stuff: strain copy, flaky tests, readiness clobber, gen5 rr, health export, sleep reject.
• Feat/step goal and calibrating rings.
• fix fabricated health-export leak, silenced-CTA bug, dedupe helpers, drop stray local files.
• repin + fix #305 + fix #40.
• fix noop import: trust CRC over size, handle real corruption honestly.

New Contributors:

• @Pablodvs made their first contribution.

What's new:

Battery.

• Background battery drain on Android significantly reduced — the app now polls your band instead of listening constantly when nothing needs live data.
• Live workout streaming pauses automatically in the background and resumes instantly when you return.
• Widgets and home-screen cards refresh only when something actually changed.

Workouts & Health sync.

• Workouts from Apple Health / Health Connect now import automatically (on by default — tap the refresh icon to grant access the first time).
• You can delete any workout from your history, recorded or imported; deleted imports won't come back.
• The import control moved to the top of the workout list.

Sleep & Health export.

• Apple Health now receives your full sleep session, including light-sleep stages that were previously missing.
• Fixed: editing or re-syncing a night could leave stale fragments behind in Apple Health.
• Fixed: "time not worn" is no longer exported as awake time.

Journal.

• Custom trackers are back — add your own items (supplements, habits, anything with a number) to the daily journal.
• Your custom items are included in correlations and weekly findings like built-in ones.
• Duplicate or failed entries are now handled cleanly instead of overwriting existing data.

Reminders & notifications.

• Medication reminders with an optional buzz on the band.
• Get-up-and-move nudge, wind-down reminder before your learned bedtime, daily check-in prompt, step-goal alert.
• Weekly summary notification when the week actually found something.
• Low-battery alert threshold is now adjustable in settings.
• "Did you work out?" prompt works again, and every notification type has its own switch.

Scores & accuracy.

• Readiness bands recalibrated — 50 is now the middle of the scale, not a warning.
• Imported historical data no longer skews your personal baselines (your data re-scores once after updating).
• Skin temperature can now contribute to readiness when the reading is reliable.
• Sleep never re-stages to a shorter night than already saved.

Devices & connectivity.

• Improved connection reliability for WHOOP 5 / MG.
• Faster, more robust syncing with per-command confirmation.
• Fixed: double-tap gestures lost their settings picker; it's rebuilt with more actions including log water.

Fixes & polish.

• ~40 fixes across widgets, imports, exports, and UI — including stale widget data, workout maps missing on some phones, a wellness screen crash from one bad value, and general performance smoothing.

Note: the battery improvements are based on a code-level audit; if your screen-on time or standby drain looks off, tell us.

• the device dead end, imported baselines, stale screens, widgets, prompts, double-tap.
• delete the things that were only ever measuring themselves.
• repin analytics for the stager pass.
• gen5 link conformance: official bootstrap, a real burst count gate, command correlation.
• Wire the dormant notification surface (sedentary, meds buzz, battery threshold, recovery, step goal, wind-down, weekly lookback).
• fix(health): rewrite Apple Health sleep as one in-bed night (Core + stale samples).
• Cut idle battery drain on Android + replace hand-rolled logic with platform/stdlib equivalents.
• journal: bring back 'Track something else' (#273).
• Opt-in auto-import of Health workouts.

New Contributors:

• @DropTabl made their first contribution.
• @ignaciojuarez made their first contribution.
• @cbarrado made their first contribution.

rebuilt the whole app. every screen. same data, less clutter.

the ai coach actually does things now — ask it about your sleep or last tuesday, or just tell it to log your food, workout, water, mood, meds.

scan a barcode, the food goes in. works in any country.

import from apple health or health connect. your details, and old workouts with their routes.

rings on the home screen — recovery, strain, sleep.

breakdown of your day: one screen, the whole day on a timeline.

every screen opens on any past day now, not just today.

live heart rate, on the heart rate screen and your band's page.

water finally has a − as well as a +.

also: naps, an observations log, a rough night card, steps on activities and share cards,. cycle tracking is opt-in, switch it on in profile.

New icon.

some of your numbers will move. resting hr is measured only while you're asleep now, day coverage is worked out against the whole day instead of the hours you happened to be wearing it, and hours the band was off your wrist show up as gaps instead of quietly counting as zero. if today has no reading you'll see that, instead of last night's number pretending to be today's.

whoop 4, 5 and MG are all one testflight group now. no more separate whoop 5 beta.

whoop 5 and MG are still experimental. they work. expect rough edges.

widgets might be weird after a rebuild this size, and the live activity is still the old design. both next release.

and some fresh bugs, so there's something to fix next week.

privacy.NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription: OpenStrap connects to your WHOOP band over Bluetooth to sync your health data.
privacy.NSBluetoothPeripheralUsageDescription: OpenStrap connects to your WHOOP band over Bluetooth to sync your health data.
privacy.NSCameraUsageDescription: OpenStrap uses the camera to read the barcode on a food packet, so logging a meal does not mean typing its nutrition panel out by hand. It reads the barcode digits and nothing else — no photo is taken, kept, or sent anywhere.
privacy.NSHealthShareUsageDescription: OpenStrap reads your height, weight, date of birth and sex to set up your profile; your resting heart rate so it has a starting baseline; any blood pressure, blood glucose or body temperature readings, so a device that is cleared to measure those can sit beside your own data with that device's name on it — never blended into an OpenStrap number; and your workouts and their routes, so a run recorded by another app can be listed and drawn on a map here, named with the app that recorded it and never counted as one OpenStrap measured. It also reads back its own recent samples so it never writes duplicates.
privacy.NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription: OpenStrap writes your sleep, resting heart rate, HRV, respiratory rate, energy and workouts into Apple Health.
privacy.NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescrip: OpenStrap never needs always-on location and does not ask for it. It records your route only while a run, ride or walk is actively running — including when your screen is locked — and stops as soon as you finish. Your route stays on this device and is never uploaded.
privacy.NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription: OpenStrap records your route during a run, ride or walk so you can see it, colored by heart-rate zone, when the workout ends. Recording continues while your screen is locked or you switch apps, but only while a workout is running — it stops the moment you finish. Your route stays on this device and is never uploaded.
privacy.NSMotionUsageDescription: OpenStrap counts your daily steps from this iPhone's own motion chip, because a band on your wrist cannot tell walking from stirring a pot, and the phone in your pocket can. It reads step counts only — never your location or anything else the motion chip records — and only the last few days of them. Your steps stay on this device and are never uploaded.
privacy.NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription: OpenStrap does not access your photo library. This permission is linked by a dependency but unused — importing your own exported WHOOP data uses the Files app, not Photos.

Vartagram Source Code Compilation Guide:

We welcome all developers to use our source code to create applications. There are several things we require from all developers for the moment.

Creating your Telegram Application:

• Please remember to publish your code too in order to comply with the licences.

Adjust Configuration:

• Generate a random identifier:.

• Open Keychain Access and navigate to Certificates. Locate Apple Development: your@email.address (XXXXXXXXXX) and double tap the certificate. Under Details, locate Organizational Unit. This is the Team ID.
• Edit build-system/template_minimal_development_configuration.json. Use data from the previous steps.

Xcode:

• Copy and edit build-system/appstore-configuration.json.
• Generate an Xcode project:.

IPA:

• Repeat the steps from the previous section. Use distribution provisioning profiles.

FFmpeg-ios is a local audio and video processing tool that runs on iPhone and iPad, suitable for users who need to perform video to audio conversion, audio format conversion, video compression, clip cropping, volume adjustment, and media information viewing.

About:

Seanime Tenji is a mobile and TV client app for your Seanime media server with a built-in player and offline support for streaming anime and reading manga.

Seanime Tenji does not provide, host, or distribute any media content. Users are responsible for obtaining media through legal means and complying with their local laws.

Features:

• Cross-platform: Available on Android, AndroidTV, iOS and tvOS.
• Built-in media player: Powered by libmpv, supports most anime codecs and formats.
• Playback Options: Support for server local files, torrent, debrid and online streaming.

• External Player Support: Support for opening media in mobile external players such as VLC, MX Player, Outplayer, etc.

Development:

Seanime Tenji is built with React Native and Expo. Detailed guides on setup and local development workflows can be found in the Contributing Guide.

apps.subtitle: Logging in may break at random due to Apple's constant server-side changes
apps.localizedDescription:
Logging in may break at random due to Apple's constant server-side changes. If login fails, make sure that you're on the latest version of PancakeStore. Do NOT open any issues or ask for support regading logins. It will not speed up the process of fixing authentication.

Before you continue...:

• Not only is authentication unstable, but there is no guarantee that user data will be retained when downgrading! Use this tool at your own risk.

versions.localizedDescription:
EoL Notice:

PancakeStore is officially EoL (End-of-Life) as of 8/22/2026.

Apple has implemented server-side changes to the iTunes API that's used in PancakeStore, as well as other popular tools such as ipatool, which primarily include SEP-based device attestation. What this means, in short, is that PancakeStore will not work ever again unless someone figures out an alternative route for downgrading apps, or successfully re-implements the attestation logic (both of which are very difficult).

In the event that this occurs, or a new method for downgrading apps is discovered and made, we will update PancakeStore. Until then, consider the project EoL.

Thank you all for all of your support of this tool, and we apologize that things have to halt like this.

❤️.

# Original release notes.

This update mainly focuses on localizations, but we recommend updating nonetheless.

## Localizations.

We've added full localization for the following languages:

• Spanish (@isacucho).
• Arabic (@neonmodder123).
• Dutch (@jurre111).
• Vietnamese (@MineTurtlee).
• Italian (@tiziodied).
• Swedish (@nxtcoreee3).
• Romanian (@nxtcoreee3).
• Norwegian (@nxtcoreee3).

As you can see, lots more languages compared to just over a day ago. We are very thankful for all of our volunteer translators for their contributions and assistance.

## Changes.

• Added new Translators section to the Credits list.
• Very minor backend adjustments.

Thank you everybody for your patience and support! Happy downgrading!

Use this tool at your own risk! You may lose app data, and other damage could occur.

We've added full localization for the following languages:

• Russian (@gerdaroot, #2).
• German (@rooootdev).
• Chinese, Simplified (@TrollStoreX, #3).

Translations have been a goal for a long time, and we're very excited in taking the first steps to implement them. At the moment, we have not arranged a system to widely crowdsource translations for our projects, so translations will be on a one-off individually-contributed basis. This will hopefully change in the short future.

Changes:

• Fixed authentication again again again. If you were running into "failed to get pod" errors, they should be resolved now.
• Some UI changes. UI is cleaner now i think.? I know some changes were done to it. Should be more better now.
• Minor project updates. Surprisingly, the version number now says 1.3 instead of 1.2.2. If anybody predicts and leaks the next version number I'm going to be very upset.

Thank you everybody for your patience and support! Attention has been on some other projects for a bit, but we do have plenty more features to add to PancakeStore still. Stay tuned for all that. Happy downgrading!

Use this tool at your own risk! You may lose app data, and other damage could occur.

Changes:

• Improved URL handling. Authentication was broken for some people due to my poor choices in programming the URL handling. Now it should be more reliable hopefully. Brazil fix.
• Improved buttons. The buttons have been bugged for a while where you have to tap on the text for them to work, now they should be normal. Shoutout to everybody whose problems were solved by "you have to tap the text".
• Minor project updates. The version number now says 1.2.2 instead of 1.2.1. Also some small codebase cleanup.

Thank you everybody for your patience and support! Working slowly to make things more stable, hopefully less impatient complaints make their way to us.

apps.name: Stable Action
apps.subtitle: Samsung Super Steady Horizon Lock - rebuilt for iPhone
apps.localizedDescription:
Overview:

Samsung's Galaxy S26 Ultra ships a feature called Super Steady with Horizon Lock that keeps your footage perfectly level no matter how much you tilt or shake the phone. It's one of the most impressive stabilisation tricks in mobile cameras right now - and it was exclusive to Android.

Stable Action brings that exact same experience to iOS. Point it at anything, tilt your wrist, run, jump, ride - the horizon stays locked flat, just like on the S26 Ultra. Built entirely in native Swift, runs 100% on-device, no subscriptions, no cloud.

apps.subtitle: A lightweight, privacy-focused YouTube client for iOS built entirely with UIKit. No ads, no tracking, no dependencies
apps.localizedDescription:
Opaline:

A lightweight, native YouTube client for iOS 12+. No ads, no tracking, no dependencies.

Opaline was released as YTLite until August. It was renamed to avoid confusion with an unrelated tweak of the same name and is not related to it.

Screenshots follow your GitHub theme — the app supports both light and dark mode.

Why:

When Google dropped support for the official YouTube app on older devices, there was no way to watch videos properly. Browsers capped quality at 360p — and even that barely ran. Opaline was born to restore what was lost: high-quality playback on hardware that still works fine, just ignored by Google — a focused, lightweight client that does one thing well.

apps.name: VNDS
apps.subtitle: A visual novel player for iOS
apps.localizedDescription:
VNDS-LOVE-TOUCH:

VNDS-LOVE-TOUCH is a fork of VNDS-LOVE designed to work with touchscreens, particularly iPadOS devices.

VNDS-LOVE is a cross platform program that plays Visual Novel Dual Screen formatted novels. Many famous visual novels have been ported to this format, which was designed for the Nintendo DS.

What is VNDS?:

VNDS novels only have a few commands. As such, they don't have any support for animations, videos, or other fancier graphical capabilites of newer visual novels. They support basic audio and image based storytelling.

Project Status:

Mostly functional. There are no known VNDS related bugs. Note that some features from other visual novel engines might be missing. If they are, file an issue along with a general description of the feature.

apps.name: DreamPlayer
apps.subtitle: DreamPlayer is a cross-platform video player for Android, iOS/iPad, and Android TV — built for true Dolby Vision, HDR10/HDR10+, and lossless audio playback
apps.localizedDescription:
DreamPlayer:

DreamPlayer is a cross-platform video player for Android, iOS/iPad, and Android TV — built for true Dolby Vision, HDR10/HDR10+, and lossless audio playback.

This build is distributed by an independent third party and is not officially affiliated with the upstream DreamPlayer project.

Dolby Vision & HDR:

• True Dolby Vision playback on supported displays.
• HDR10 and HDR10+ dynamic metadata support.
• Native display headroom scaling and accurate color rendering.

Audio:

• Lossless audio decoding for all major codecs: DTS, DTS-HD, E-AC3, TrueHD, AC3, FLAC, and AAC.
• Multi-channel audio passthrough support.

Network Streaming:

• High-throughput streaming over SMB / Windows shares / NAS.
• WebDAV streaming with self-signed certificate support.
• FTP and SFTP streaming.
• Jellyfin and Emby direct playback with mDNS auto-discovery.
• UPnP and DLNA server browsing and playback.

versions.localizedDescription:
What's new in DreamPlayer 0.4.4:

Bug-fix release: movie folders (bookmarked to the home screen) now open as movies with a Play bar, SMB bookmarked folders play through Media3, the foreground-service crash on movie Play is fixed, release-group-heavy folder names resolve their TMDB match via the files inside (issue #11), and manual Fix-match pins survive automatic reprocessing.

Fixed:

• Movie folders play through Media3, not a bogus mpv fallback — a movie bookmarked to the home screen from an SMB/WebDAV share carried its smb://… URI in the video's path field with uri: null. The native player wrapped any path in File(.), turning smb:// into a nonexistent file:///smb:/… URI → Media3 terminal error → automatic (and wrong) fallback to the mpv engine. Fix: schemeOrFileUri in ExoPlayerView.kt parses paths that already carry an explicit scheme (smb://, http(s)://, ftp://, content://) as real URIs routed to the matching DataSource (SmbDataSource/OkHttp/content resolver); plain filesystem paths still become file://. The movie entry is also built as smb://<serverId>/<share>/<rel> so SmbStore.resolve finds the saved credentials.
• Red-screen "null" flash when opening a movie folder — tmd_details_screen.dart built the movie-folder Play bar with _folderMovieEntry!; with a cached TMDB movie match but the SMB listing still in flight, _isMovieFolder was true while _folderMovieEntry was null, so Flutter threw for a few frames until the listing landed. Fix: the Play bar/info cards render only once the entry resolves.

• Manual Fix-match pins are no longer silently lost — TmdMeta gained a manual flag persisted through the cache; resolve/resolveFolder return the pinned entry untouched for manual keys (automatic matching, folder scans, and home refreshes never overwrite them), and only clear/Remove-info removes them. series_seasons_screen._fixMatch and tmd_details_screen._fixMatch stamp the flag when the user picks a match.
• "Remove info" on a home card no longer re-fetches the same poster — after Remove-info, a home refresh/relaunch re-resolved the key and silently fetched the same match back. TmdService now keeps a persistent suppression set (dreamplayer.tmdbSuppressed): Remove-info suppresses the key, resolve/resolveFolder return null while suppressed (card stays a placeholder), and only an explicit Fix match (or a fresh folder add → new key) lifts it. _removeInfo call sites in tmd_details_screen.dart and series_seasons_screen.dart use it.
• Home no longer churns existing movie matches — _resolveFolderMetadata re-resolved every folder whose cached match had folderSeason == null, which hit every movie folder on every load and could silently swap an auto match. Movie-kind matches are left alone; only null or incomplete TV matches get re-resolved.
• Folder with subdirectories never hides them behind the series view (SMB) — the SMB (and now guarded) series detection could trigger on a folder that also contains season subfolders, hiding the directories behind an episode-only list. isSeries now requires the folder to contain video files and no subfolders (dirEntries.isEmpty), so a top-level series folder with Season 1/… subfolders stays in the flat browsable list.
• SMB focus highlight no longer jumps across files — after tapping a directory, Flutter's ListView re-created children and auto-focused whatever landed at the same index (the tapped dir became a video file). A post-frame FocusManager.instance.primaryFocus?.unfocus after the list rebuild prevents the jump, and the tree/list keys are ValueKey('smb-$share-$path') per location.
• Get Info search dialog no longer overflows in landscape — the search results ListView was Flexible, so the AlertDialog's fixed-width Column overflowed the short landscape viewport ("bottom overflowed by 60 pixels"). Content is now a SingleChildScrollView with the results list height-capped at 40% of the screen.
• Fix match no longer crashes from folder mode — _computeParentFolderName dereferenced widget.video!.path even when opening the dialog from a folder (where widget.video is null); an early return now guards it.
• Fix match / Remove info buttons moved below the overview — previously pinned to the screen bottom where they could be missed (especially after scrolling metadata); they now sit directly under the synopsis, and the Remove-info button uses the error color.

Added:

• Movie folders open as movies on the home screen — a folder group whose TMDB match is a movie now opens the movie details screen (backdrop hero, poster, overview) with a bottom Play/Resume bar instead of a lone-file series view ("Episode 1" with no way to play it). Per-engine resume (media3/mpv) and last-engine memory are shown on the same "Resume from m:ss" bar. TMDB movie images.backdrops are now fetched into the details model for a stills gallery row.
• Movie-first resolution for standalone-movie folders — bestForQuery gained preferMovie; folders whose listed files show no SxxEyy/episode evidence resolve to a movie before a TV show (and the trailing Title 2/Title 3 numbered-sequel candidates are tried) so movie folders don't mis-pin to the TMDB series/collection entry.

Pick the APK for your device and allow "Install unknown apps" when prompted:

Not sure which to pick? Grab the Universal APK.

The DreamPlayer-<version>.ipa in this release is unsigned — Apple only allows app installation through the App Store / TestFlight, so the IPA must be signed with your own (free) Apple ID. It's quick:

• Install SideStore or AltStore on your iPhone/iPad (sidestore.io / altstore.io).

• Open SideStore/AltStore → + → select DreamPlayer-<version>.ipa. It signs it with your Apple ID and installs.
• The signature lasts 7 days; SideStore/AltStore auto-refresh it in the background over WiFi — a weekly open is all that's needed.

Notes:

• A free Apple ID can keep ~3 sideloaded apps active per device.
• First-time setup of SideStore/AltStore needs a computer (or a second Apple device).

Versioning:

App version follows semver, bumped per release (current release: 0.4.0).

Playing videos from your NAS / SMB share:

DreamPlayer plays NAS files through the Files app's built-in SMB support and "Open with".

• iPhone/iPad: Files → ⋯ → Connect to Server → enter smb://<address> → browse to a video → long-press → Share → Open in "DreamPlayer". Prefer a folder? Bookmark it once: home + → Add folder to library → your NAS folder.
• Android: CX Explorer → Open with → DreamPlayer (streams over CX's local HTTP proxy).

versions.localizedDescription:
v0.8.0:

📅 Released June 20, 2026.

qBittorrent:

Full qBittorrent support lands in Seekarr — the headline feature of this release.

• 🧲 Torrent management: list, detail view, and full lifecycle control (start/pause/delete/edit).

🧪 Tests:
