apps.name: Applesauce
apps.subtitle: A playful emulator for iOS. Plays supported 32-bit iPhone games on iOS 15+ — no jailbreak needed, though JIT is. An unaffiliated fork of touchHLE and HyperHLE; neither project endorses it
apps.localizedDescription:
Applesauce:

A playful emulator for iOS. It plays supported 32-bit iPhone games on modern iPhones — no jailbreak required, though JIT is. It installs and runs on iPadOS too, but every game runs as an iPhone guest for now: the core's iPad device families are not yet reachable from the app.

Applesauce is an unaffiliated fork. The emulation is entirely the work of touchHLE and its fork HyperHLE; this project is the iOS app built around them — the interface, the build system and the packaging. Neither project is connected to Applesauce or endorses it, so please report problems here rather than to them. No games or Apple software are included.

versions.localizedDescription:
Applesauce 0.4.1:

This update improves the library, game-session cleanup and AltStore Classic distribution. It keeps the same bundle identifier as 0.4.0, so it updates an existing Applesauce installation and retains its library and saves.

In AltStore Classic, open Sources → + and add:

Choose Applesauce from the source. Future releases appear in AltStore; you do not have to download a new IPA manually each time. Signing, refresh and JIT requirements still apply. The source does not enable JIT automatically.

Full installation and JIT guide.

Fixes:

• Importing copies files away from the main UI thread and coordinates access with Files providers such as iCloud Drive. A failed copy is cleaned up before it can appear as a partially imported game.
• Repeated taps cannot queue overlapping game launches. Library reloads are also suppressed while a game or import is active.
• Malformed game metadata that causes the HyperHLE parser to panic is caught at the native bridge. The library uses this parser regardless of the chosen gameplay core and falls back to a filename when metadata is unreadable.
• The FPS timer no longer retains the game-controls screen after exiting.
• The exit button respects the screen's safe area, and returning to the library uses the iOS 15 orientation fallback too.

• Building a second core copies only that core, avoiding accidental overwrite of a newer core with a stale file from another checkout.

• Migration instructions include saves and correctly explain which settings need to be reselected.

The AltStore source is checked against the unsigned IPA's version, build, minimum iOS, size, checksum and permissions. A release workflow updates the source for future published releases; prereleases and TrollStore packages are excluded from that automatic update.

Downloads:

• Applesauce-iOS-unsigned.ipa: AltStore Classic and other ordinary sideloaders.
• Applesauce-iOS-trollstore.ipa: the existing TrollStore route for supported older iOS devices, with JIT enabled through TrollStore.
• Applesauce-iOS-trollstore-permanent-jit.ipa: A11 and older only. Do not install this variant on A12 or newer devices.

The emulator versions remain HyperHLE v1.0.6 and touchHLE 0.2.3. This release does not claim additional game compatibility or fix the known Sims Medieval.

fresh device regression testing of 0.4.1 is still needed.

No games are included. Full credit for emulation belongs to touchHLE and HyperHLE. Applesauce is an independent, unofficial port.

Applesauce 0.4.0:

This release renames the app. What was touchHLE for iOS is now Applesauce — a playful emulator for iOS. The name, icon and identifier are new; the emulation is the same as 0.3.0, plus the fixes below.

Applesauce is an unaffiliated fork. The emulation is entirely the work of touchHLE and its fork HyperHLE, and neither project is connected to this one or endorses it. Please report problems here rather than to them.

Read this first: your games do not move automatically:

The bundle identifier changed, so Applesauce installs alongside the old app with an empty library rather than replacing it.

• Open Files and go to On My iPhone.
• Find the old app's folder — HyperHLE if you had 0.2.0 or 0.3.0, touchHLE if you had 0.1.0.
• Move touchHLE_apps from it into the Applesauce folder. Move touchHLE_sandbox too if you want your saves.
• Delete the old app.

App-wide settings do not come across; set them again under Settings.

The deployment target drops from 17.4 to 15.0, and there are now three IPAs:

The TrollStore builds carry the memory entitlements that let older hardware map the emulator's 4GiB guest address space. A free Apple account cannot sign those, which is why this is a TrollStore route rather than a sideloading one.

The permanent-JIT build crashes on launch on A12 and newer (iPhone XS/XR onwards) — iOS 15 bans the entitlement it carries. Use the ordinary TrollStore build there.

iOS 15 and 16 are untested by this project. The support is back-ported from nerivalaitis' work, tested by them on iOS 15. Reports from those versions are the most useful thing you can send.

Fixes:

• A game no longer dies when a rotation is refused. A guest asking to rotate while the host UI still has the old orientation pinned used to panic and take the whole game down mid-play; it now logs a warning and carries on.
• Black screen after rotating, on games without a fullscreen layer. SDL recreates its framebuffer object when the window leaves and re-enters fullscreen, and compositing kept using the one cached at startup.
• A crash inside the emulator no longer wedges the app. Panics were unwinding across the FFI boundary, leaving a black screen and a dead exit button with nothing in the log; they are now caught and reported.
• Guest memory allocation falls back instead of failing outright when iOS refuses the full read-write mapping, which is what blocked older devices.
• JIT detection understands permanent JIT. A TrollStore install with dynamic-codesigning was previously told it had no JIT, and had to use "Start Anyway" every time.
• Portrait is selectable under Settings → Starting Orientation, for games that declare landscape but draw portrait anyway.
• The previous run's log is kept as touchhle-host-previous.log, so force-quitting a hung game no longer destroys the log that recorded the hang.

Both emulator cores carry these fixes.

Credits:

• touchHLE — the original emulator.as the default core.
• nerivalaitis — the iOS 15 back-port, TrollStore packaging and the memory-allocation fallback.

touchHLE for iOS 0.3.0:

One app, two emulator cores. HyperHLE and touchHLE now ship together, and you choose which one runs each game. Neither is strictly better — HyperHLE runs more games, including The Sims Medieval, while some titles only work on touchHLE 0.2.3.

What's New:

• Both cores in one app — HyperHLE v1.0.6 and touchHLE 0.2.3.
• A core per game — touch and hold a game in your library to choose its core. Settings sets the default for everything else.
• JIT is checked before a game starts. With JIT off the app used to close the instant a game launched, which looked like the game crashing. Now it says so.

Upgrading:

Replaces the HyperHLE 0.2.0 app in place. The separate touchHLE 0.1.0 app is no longer needed and can be deleted once this is installed.

Install:

Sideload touchHLE-HyperHLE-iOS-unsigned.ipa with AltStore Classic or similar, then enable JIT with StikDebug + LocalDevVPN. JIT must be enabled again every time the app starts as a new process.

Games are not included — bring your own decrypted 32-bit IPA.

Tested on an iPhone 16 Pro running iOS 27 beta 4 (24A5390f). Not an official release of touchHLE or of HyperHLE, and neither project endorses it.

apps.name: DukeX
apps.subtitle: Xbox Emulation on iOS
apps.localizedDescription:
DukeX is an experimental iOS and macOS frontend for xemu. The iOS build embeds the xemu core in a native Swift shell and presents the Vulkan renderer through MoltenVK and native Metal presentation. The macOS build packages a nested desktop Xemu fork inside a Mac Catalyst DukeX experience.

DukeX does not include Xbox system files, game images, or signing certificates. Users and testers are required to provide their own legally obtained files. DukeX is intended solely for legitimate emulation and preservation purposes, and is not designed for use with pirated materials.

At a Glance:

• Runtime: TCG with version-aware JIT setup; iOS 26 or later uses the StikDebug Universal.js flow.

versions.localizedDescription:
DukeX v1.0.2 - Expanding the Xbox Experience:

DukeX v1.0.2 is our biggest step yet toward preserving the full original Xbox experience, not just the games. This release introduces the first native macOS build, expands XB.Live integration, and brings richer community features to both iOS and macOS.

What's New:

• XB.Live Rich Presence and playtime tracking: friends can see what you are playing while DukeX tracks supported playtime sessions.
• XB.Live messaging: threaded conversations, friend messaging, unread indicators, supported game invites, and existing Xbox inbox support now live inside DukeX.
• XB.Live social expansion: friend requests, friend management, online presence, and deeper community integration are available from the Profile experience.
• Activity Feed: XB.Live news, friend online status, friend achievement unlocks, and community updates now appear in a continuously refreshed timeline.
• Controller Landscape Mode: on iOS, compatible controllers can switch DukeX into a controller-first browsing and launch experience.
• Expanded AirPlay and external display support: big-screen play is more reliable across supported display configurations.

Improvements:

• Improved achievements with Games, Apps, and Cores grouping plus updated artwork handling for XB.Live Core, DukeX Core, and special test titles.
• Improved game tile spacing and cover handling across iOS and macOS.
• Improved XB.Live cloud-save sync metadata with console identity v2, content-hash dedupe, and server-assisted cross-console restore handling.
• Fixed achievement progress rounding so time-based achievements do not show 100% before they are actually complete.

Availability:

• iOS: install DukeX.v1.0.2.ipa through StikStore, SideStore, or another supported sideloading workflow.
• macOS: install DukeX.macOS.v1.0.2.dmg by dragging DukeX to Applications.
• Hardware requirements on iOS remain Apple A14 Bionic or Apple M1 hardware or newer.
• iOS 16.0 or later is supported, with iOS 16 support remaining experimental.

Important:

DukeX does not include Xbox system files, game images, BIOS files, copyrighted content, signing certificates, or user games. Users must provide their own legally obtained files. DukeX is intended for legitimate emulation, preservation, testing, and personal library use.

DukeX v1.0.1 brings Xbox Live profile groundwork, improved rendering stability, Touch Controls, AirPlay, personalization, cover art scraping, and native URL scheme support.

What's New:

• Partnership with XB.Live introduces profile integration for achievements, friends, messages, community events, and cloud sync support.
• Core rendering and performance handling have been improved for better stability across more titles.
• Touch Controls now support .manicskin layouts, .deltaskin and .gammaskin imports, haptic feedback, and the official DukeX Default skin.
• AirPlay support lets compatible devices send gameplay to larger displays.
• Themes, automatic cover art retrieval, and DukeX URL scheme support expand personalization and launch-link workflows.
• Minimum iOS support has been experimentally lowered to iOS 16 on A14/M1 or newer hardware.

Known Issue:

DukeX does not include Xbox system files, game images, BIOS files, or copyrighted content. Users must provide their own legally obtained files.

DukeX v1.0.0 is the first release build prepared for wider sideload testing.

Highlights:

• Native SwiftUI game library, profile, and settings interface.
• Game-library sorting by Favorites, Title, Live support, and Recent.
• Per-game favorite toggles from the long-press menu.
• Portrait and landscape library column controls.
• Insignia-oriented NAT defaults and live indicators for supported titles.
• User-accessible BIOS, ROMs, Covers, GameConfigs, and ShaderCaches folders.
• Per-game cover art, custom config import, shader-cache clearing, and dashboard launch.
• Built-in FPS/system statistics HUD and app-owned launch logs.
• iOS 18.0+ install target with version-aware JIT behavior.

User Notes:

• This IPA is unsigned and intended for sideload signing tools.
• DukeX does not include Xbox system files, game images, BIOS files, HDD images, or signing certificates.
• Users and testers must provide their own legally obtained files.
• iOS 18.x uses W^X reprotection after JIT has been enabled for the DukeX process.
• iOS 26 or later requires StikDebug with Universal.js assigned to com.mafty.dukex.
• Rendering correctness and performance are still title- and device-dependent.
• Apple's Metal HUD may not appear with the current presenter; use DukeX's built-in stats HUD for testing.

apps.name: Nyxian
apps.subtitle: IDE to develop native code iOS apps and utilities on stock iOS it self just via a certificate and a custom micro kernel for those apps
apps.localizedDescription:
What is it?:

Nyxian is an iOS app that empowers developers with a full toolchain they can use while even being offline for iOS development on iPhone. It supports Swift, C, Objective-C, C++ and Objective-C++. It’s a powerful IDE that made the impossible possible, a fully on-device iOS IDE that doesn’t even need a cloud and can even be used with airplane mode enabled after it downloaded the SDK and resources from our server. It supports officially iOS 18.0 all the way up to the latest iOS version (iOS/iPadOS 27.0 tested). You can compile and run iOS apps on the go with ease, using the entire iOS 26.5 SDK.

apps.name: Locus
apps.subtitle: Free open-source iPhone location teleport (MIT)
apps.localizedDescription:
Locus:

Free and open-source iPhone location teleport. Tap the map, search a place, or drive a route — Locus injects coordinates through Apple’s developer location service into locationd, so Maps and other apps see the spoofed GPS (not just a Wi‑Fi lookup that outdoor GPS will overwrite).

Features:

• One-tap teleport (map pin or place search).
• Live joystick — walk / run / cycle / drive with light speed variation.
• Walk/Drive routing on real roads & footpaths (MapKit).
• Draw a path or import / export GPX.
• Background keep-alive + live status bar + drop alerts.
• Favorites & recents.
• First-run setup walkthrough.
• Fully on-device — no analytics, nothing uploaded.

Install:

Bundle ID: com.chrismack.locus.

versions.localizedDescription:

• Pairing file picker — selecting an RPPairing .plist in the importer works again (reported broken on iOS 26 when taps did nothing).
• LiveContainer — added Paste RPPairing from clipboard, plus README/SETUP notes for Fix File Picker and Share → Locus.

Install:

Sideload Locus-1.0.2.ipa with Feather, SideStore, AltStore, Sideloadly, or LiveContainer.

See SETUP.md for pairing and LocalDevVPN.

Bundle ID: com.chrismack.locus.

Locus 1.0.0:

First public release — free MIT open-source iPhone location teleport.

Highlights:

• Map teleport, joystick, routes & GPX.
• On-device pairing (iOS 27) or RPPairing import.
• First-run setup + LocalDevVPN deep link.
• Icon Composer split-pin app icon.

Install:

See SETUP.md for pairing and LocalDevVPN.

Bundle ID: com.chrismack.locus.

privacy.NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription: Locus uses the local network to advertise as a pairable host (iOS 27 pairing) and to reach the developer tunnel (LocalDevVPN) for GPS override.
privacy.NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescrip: Locus keeps a light location session alive so simulated GPS can stay active in the background.
privacy.NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription: Locus uses your real location so you can aim the map and return home after teleporting.

apps.name: Ready
apps.subtitle: A Home Computer Emulator for iPad
apps.localizedDescription:
With preliminary support for these computers:

• Commander X16.

It is based on atari800, fuse, Vice, and x16-emulator, which provide accurate emulation of many hardware variants and peripherals.

It requires at least iPadOS 13.5.

It aims to approximate the feeling of using actual hardware:

• Rather than configuring abstract settings, you select hardware components.
• The software keyboard is a facsimile of the original, reflecting the different existing styles.
• Even the noise of the disk drive is emulated.

The Library section offers a way to organize a large collection of games, demos and programs. The emulated hardware can be customized for each entry.

The Inbox provides a place to quickly try new programs. You can easily move the ones you want to keep to the library.

apps.name: Dusklight
apps.subtitle: Dusklight brings a classic adventure to PC and mobile platforms with a variety of fixes and improvements
apps.localizedDescription:
Overview:

Dusklight is a reverse-engineered reimplementation of Twilight Princess.

It aims to be as accurate as possible to the original while also providing new options, enhancements, and tools to customize your experience.

Setup:

Dusklight does not provide any copyrighted assets. You must provide your own copy of the original game.

At a minimum, Dusklight requires a GPU with support for D3D12, Vulkan 1.1+, or Metal. For older devices, best-effort support is provided for D3D11 and OpenGL ES (Android), but will not achieve full accuracy or performance. Your experience with specific hardware, operating systems, and drivers may vary.

• Dump your game:.

Dusklight currently supports all commercial discs except for Wii's Korean release.

versions.localizedDescription:
What's new:

• Added: Support Clawshot hanging & Hawkeye with touch controls.
• Added: Configure Android Surface.setFrameRate; improves performance on some devices.
• Fixed: Texture replacement regressions in v1.4.0 (load ordering & missing UI textures).
• Fixed: Performance regression on some GPUs (AMD on Windows in particular).

• Fixed: Hidden Dusklight menu still receiving inputs in some circumstances.
• Fixed: GPU backend fallback regression.

With the release of Dusklight, it's been our goal to raise the bar for quality and polish in ports. First, we focused our efforts on accuracy, stability and quality of life. Now, we're excited to bring some long-awaited features and improvements: full mouse controls, mobile touch controls, and a complete performance overhaul, among many others! And don't worry, we still have some even bigger features coming soon. Please stay posted!

What's new:

• Added: Mobile touch controls & customization.
• Added: Mouse control for third-person camera.
• Added: Mouse/touch support for in-game menus (disable via "Mouse/Touch in Menus" setting).
• Added: Native gyro/rumble support on Android and iOS.
• Added: Overhauled performance; up to 4x improvement on CPU-bottlenecked devices.

• We've optimized every part of the renderer, from game particles to GPU frame submission.
• Framerates should be much more stable across areas and with heavy effects.

• Added: ASTC DDS support for texture replacements.

• Texture pack authors can now ship desktop packs with BC7, and mobile packs with ASTC.

• Added: Load mipmaps from DDS files.

• Texture pack authors can now ship mipmaps within DDS files, rather than requiring separate _mip* sidecars.
• Recent Dolphin versions also support this.

• Added: "Swap Direct Select Input" option: enables Direct Select by default for item wheel.
• Added: Improved scaling for Memory Card and Name Select screens.
• Added: Individual X and Y sensitivity settings for Free Camera.
• Added: "Enable Controller LED" setting for supported controllers.
• Added: Preview when changing "Enable Texture Replacements".
• Added: "Button Fishing" QoL option from TPHD.
• Added: Interpolate most particles, fishing rod line, door chains, hookshot chains.
• Added: "Glitched" acheivements count beyond 100% completion (no longer requires Glitched for 100%).
• Added: "HUD Scale" setting for in-game HUD.
• Added: "Freeze Time" setting for debug camera.
• Added: "Restore Wii 1.0 Glitches" now restores Green Chu merging.
• Added: "Magic Armor Behavior" cheat: Normal, On Damage, Double Defense, Invincible, Cosmetic.
• Added: "Remember Window Size" setting.
• Added: Automatically initialize Memory Card when "Instant Saves" is enabled.
• Added: Automatically prune dawn_cache.db.
• Fixed: Crash when talking to the Zora under the waterfall in Zora's Domain.
• Fixed: Snowpeak avalanche not triggering with bloom disabled (yes, you read that right).
• Fixed: Hidden Village crash after getting Ilia's Charm from Impaz.
• Fixed: Monkey loading crash in Forest Temple.
• Fixed: Ganondorf's cape texture & tearing.
• Fixed: Poe Counter in Mirror Mode.
• Fixed: Respawning in final Zant fight phase.
• Fixed: Mirror mode sign arrows.

• Fixed: macOS 12 support.
• Fixed: Package Visual C++ Redistributable DLLs on Windows.

• Fixed: Texture LOD bias & sampler settings for replaced textures.
• Fixed: Crash with incorrectly-sized texture replacements.

• Changed: Remove embedded gamecontrollerdb.txt.

• This broke mappings for various controllers, notably Switch Pro controller on Android.
• The game now loads custom controller mappings from <data folder>/gamecontrollerdb.txt if manually created.

apps.name: SunPad
apps.subtitle: Super Mario Sunshine on iPhone, iPad, Apple Silicon Mac, and tVOS through static recompilation and Metal
apps.localizedDescription:
SunPad:

Super Mario Sunshine on iPhone, iPad, Apple silicon Mac, and experimental Apple TV through ahead-of-time recompilation. SunPad brings together Metal rendering, touch controls, controller support, and local game-image import. Supply your own supported copy of the game.

Built with ModernGekko, by Hyperway, ExpansionPak and contributors, and DolRecomp, on the RecompCore / Dolphin runtime. SunPad provides the Apple app and Sunshine-specific integration. See full credits, including Apple TV contributions and AI/artwork provenance.

Maintained forks: ModernGekko, RecompCore, and DolRecomp. Runtime and compiler dependencies use pinned submodules. The source graph records the separate Apple and tvOS versions.

versions.localizedDescription:
Preview 13: maintained-fork rebuild:

Fresh unsigned iPhone/iPad and experimental Apple TV IPAs, version 0.1.0 build 13. Both are rebuilt from the maintained ModernGekko, RecompCore and DolRecomp forks with exact pinned source revisions. The Apple and tvOS audio paths remain separate.

This release includes corrected upstream attribution, original dependency license texts, recursive source references, a corresponding-source archive, and a build provenance manifest. It uses the hardened package validation and output-preservation workflow. No new gameplay feature or performance improvement is claimed.

apps.name: Hotline Navigator
apps.subtitle: Official Website
apps.localizedDescription:
Hotline Navigator:

Official Website.

What the hell is Hotline?:

Hotline in concept, was to replicate a BBS but for the internet age. Modern users would recongize more as a proto peer-to-peer or a Discord like application.

Hotline's Navigator's website has a deeper drive the history of Hotline.

Platform Support:

Right now the iOS, iPadOS, and Android versions are not in their respective app stores and must be built manually or sideloaded.

This is a Tauri-based Hotline client that provides a modern, cross-platform experience for the classic Hotline protocol. Built with React and Rust, it offers:

• Cross-Platform: Single codebase for macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, iPadOS, and Android.
• Modern Stack: React + TypeScript frontend, Rust backend.

• Native Performance: Tauri's lightweight architecture for fast, efficient apps.

versions.localizedDescription:
v0.2.8:

There's been a lot of rapid changes in Navigator's capabilities so this release UX quality-of-life series of fixes since the Discord style chat introduced a new UX paradigm which inevitable had some loose ends.

Disconnects are detected in seconds instead of minutes, chat icons no longer fall back to gray letter placeholders for emotes or for users who chatted before their info loaded, and! / / commands now appear above the bot's response instead of below it. News browsing also works on multi-tier servers like VesperNet, where top-level entries are folders of folders.

Next release will be new feature bound.

Bugfixes and Improvements:

• Faster disconnect detection — When a server vanishes silently (peer crash, network drop, NAT timeout), the client now notices in ~60s on macOS/Linux and ~130s on Windows, down from the OS TCP retransmit default of 15+ minutes. Auto-reconnect kicks in correspondingly faster.

• News browsing on nested servers — On servers like VesperNet where the top-level news entries are folders containing more folders, navigation no longer dead-ends with an empty article pane. The client now dispatches based on the clicked item's actual type (bundle vs. category) rather than assuming any non-root path holds articles.

Technical:

• TCP SO_KEEPALIVE configured on the control channel via socket2: idle=30s, interval=10s, retries=3 on macOS/Linux. Windows uses the OS default retry count.
• App-level keepalive failure now emits StatusChanged(Disconnected) and clears the transport, instead of silently breaking.

• Optimistic insert tagged with pending: true and optimisticKey; echo dedup matches by userName + message text within a 10s window. /me and /em are preformatted as *** name action to match the server echo. 30s safety timeout clears the pending flag if no echo arrives.
• News load effect dispatches on a tracked newsLeafType (2 = bundle → get_news_categories; 3 = category → get_news_articles). Going back always sets leaf type to bundle, since non-leaf path segments are bundles by invariant.

Installation:

Download the installer for your platform from the release assets.

.dmg = macOS, .msi/.exe = Windows, .apk = Android, .ipa = iOS/iPadOS, Linux hippies can figure it out.

v0.2.7:

This is a pretty big upgrade and allows servers to add chat history. Anyone writing their own server can always yank Navigator and run the tauri in dev mode as there's a ton of debugging that is exposed.

Also hardened link preview fetching against SSRF, added a link preview toggle, and fixed download filename collisions.

As writing this the only server that has chat history is Apple Media Archive as it's the only hotline server I run.

New Features:

• Apple Media Archive uses HOPE --The default bookmark for Apple Media Archive now has HOPE enabled, with automatic migration for existing users.

Improvements:

• Sending a message while scrolled up through history snaps back to the bottom.

Security:

• SSRF Protection for Link Previews — Link preview fetches now validate target URLs before connecting. Private/internal IP ranges are blocked (RFC 1918, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, ULA IPv6). Only http/https schemes allowed. Redirects are followed manually with per-hop validation, preventing redirect-based SSRF attacks.

Technical:

• is_private_ip and validate_url_target for SSRF-safe link preview fetching with manual redirect following.
• Reconnect catch-up via AFTER cursor when the tab stays alive across disconnect/reconnect cycles.

An experimental, fully on-device iPhone app for backing up selected photos, videos, and albums to Google Photos. It is a single SwiftUI app that completes Google account setup in an in-app web view, so everything happens on the phone without a desktop companion or hosted service.

This project uses Google's private, undocumented Photos endpoints and an Android-style authentication flow. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google, and the integration may stop working without notice. Treat it as experimental software and use it at your own risk.

What it can do:

• Connect a Google account through Google's EmbeddedSetup flow, in an in-app web view.
• Capture the single-use oauth_token in-process from the web view's cookie store.
• Exchange the token for a Google Photos credential entirely on the device.

versions.localizedDescription:
New:

iOS gives each run about 30 seconds, so the action spends them finding and preparing photos, then leaves the uploads to iOS. With the app open it just adds to the queue — the uploads you are watching are not interrupted. Photos stored only in iCloud still wait until you open the app.

• See when iOS actually runs the backup. Settings → Support → Diagnostics → Recent Runs lists every run — opening the app, Back Up Now, Shortcuts, and the background windows iOS grants — with the time it started, how long it took, what it did, and the conditions it ran under (network, battery and charging, Low Power Mode, locked or not). Background windows also record how long after the request iOS started them.
• Event Timeline. Every decision the app makes now leaves an entry saying why: why a background run was or wasn't requested, why uploads paused, which step an upload failed at and what Google said, when an item waited for iCloud, what iOS delivered while the app was closed. It keeps two weeks of history; repeats fold into one line, and warnings and errors are kept longer than routine entries, so a big backup does not push out the one failure that matters.
• Storage. Settings → Support → Storage shows what the app keeps on your phone — pending upload copies, backup history, transfer receipts, caches — and Clean Up Unused Data removes leftovers without touching pending uploads or your account.

Fixed:

Suspending the app normally never counts against an item, so iOS closing the app in the background does not skip anything.

• The app knows when it last closed unexpectedly. If it disappears while open, while starting, or during a background run, the next launch records it and the report says so — even when iOS did not share a crash report.
• Leftover transfer receipts are cleaned up. Receipts that no upload owns any more are removed a day after they were written, and Google's responses are no longer kept in a disk cache.

Notes:

• 161 tests, 158 passing (2 opt-in live tests, and 1 Keychain test that needs a signed build, skipped).
• Checked on an iPhone 12 running iOS 17.0.3: launch, account and queue restore, background scheduling, and the event log. A background window granted by iOS overnight and a Shortcuts automation on a locked phone still need to be seen on more devices — reports from either are very welcome.
• Crash details from iOS are only included when Share With App Developers is on (Settings → Privacy & Security → Analytics & Improvements), and they arrive a day or so after the crash.
• The Simulator cannot run background uploads or schedule background tasks. Use a device to exercise real backup behaviour.

Fixed:

• "Google returned HTTP 400" during finalization now recovers instead of failing the photo. A live run against Google reproduced it: an upload whose receipt comes back without its upload token is committed anyway, Google answers "At least one valid blueprint is required", and every retry replayed the same dead receipt. The receipt is now checked where it is produced and where it is used, and a rejected one costs the item one fresh transfer rather than its whole retry budget. Receipts saved by older versions are checked too, so a queue carrying one from before the update recovers on the next attempt.
• A full Google account stops the backup and says so. It used to arrive as a generic HTTP failure, so the queue kept going and failed every remaining photo the same way, one at a time. Backup now pauses with an explanation and waits — freeing space and tapping Resume picks it back up. It does not ask you to reconnect the account, because signing in again does not free storage.
• Every upload commits under the quality setting you have selected now. The choice between original quality and Storage Saver, and whether the upload counts against your Google storage, was captured when the photo was prepared and then kept with it — so a photo prepared while Storage Saver was on kept uploading as Storage Saver after you turned it off, including after restarting the app.

Improved:

• A failed upload will tell you what Google said. Tap a failed row for the full reason, selectable, with Copy Details. Diagnostics keeps the last 25 failures with their error codes and a Copy All, and counts how many there have been — the reason used to be a two-line caption that disappeared as soon as the row was retried or cleared.
• Error messages name what failed. "Google returned HTTP 400 during finalization" rather than "check your connection", and Google's own explanation is decoded instead of shown as a hex dump.
• A long backup no longer slows down as it progresses. The activity list, navigation, and the uploads themselves got slower the further into a whole-library backup you were: the queue's counters, its row lookups, and its search for the next upload all walked the entire queue on every progress update, and the per-album "backed up" counts re-scanned every selected album on each of those too. All of it is now maintained as it goes, so the cost no longer grows with the size of the queue.

Notes:

• 132 tests, 130 passing (2 opt-in live tests skipped).

• The Simulator cannot run background uploads or schedule background tasks. Use a device to exercise real backup behaviour.

Fixed:

Back Up Now queued one page of 250 and left the rest to a loop that was gated on the same conditions as automatic scheduling — including "Automatic Backup is turned off", which is exactly what Stop Backup sets. With the toggle off that loop exited before doing anything, so the button uploaded 250 items and stopped, and the rest of the album stayed off the queue until you tapped again. Re-check Backups shares the loop and had the same cap, which is why it looked like it cleared the queue and then refilled only a fraction of it.

A manual run is you asking right now, so it no longer consults the automatic-backup toggle at all. It still stops when the app leaves the foreground, the account becomes unusable, or backup is paused.

• The whole selection now goes into the queue at once. Paging the foreground meant the queue only ever held a slice of the work. Both buttons now queue everything, and the simultaneous uploads setting decides how much of it moves at a time. Background windows keep their 250-item batch, which only bounds memory — the queue is durable, so whatever one window cannot finish waits for the next.

Notes:

• 107 tests, 104 passing (2 opt-in live tests and 1 Simulator Keychain test skipped).
• The Simulator cannot run background uploads or schedule background tasks. Use a device to exercise real backup behaviour.

apps.name: MiniWatts
apps.subtitle: An iPhone battery, charging and thermal instrument built on private iOS APIs — real charger watts, what actually reaches the cell, all 30 temperature sensors, and the USB-PD handshake
apps.localizedDescription:
MiniWatts:

English · 简体中文.

An iPhone battery and charging monitor built on Apple's private APIs. It reads the phone's own power-management sensors — the ones iOS uses to run the charge — and shows what the charger is delivering, how much of it reaches the cell, where the rest goes as heat, and what every temperature sensor in the phone is doing while it happens.

Sideload only. Private APIs mean this can never be on the App Store — you sign and install it yourself. There is no network code of any kind: nothing it reads leaves your phone.

Install:

Download the latest MiniWatts-unsigned.ipa from.

Apple ID — Sideloadly, AltStore, SideStore and Xcode all do this. A free Apple ID works; the app then expires after seven days and you re-sign it.

versions.localizedDescription:

• 实时活动加入"结束"按钮：锁屏和展开的灵动岛上都有。MiniWatts 被挂起或被划掉时，也能直接把实时活动关掉。.

修复:

New:

• Configurable floating meter: show charging power, component temperatures, or both. Temperatures can be all four at once (SoC, battery, charger, hottest) or a single one. • Selectable Live Activity reading: the compact Dynamic Island shows charging power, SoC temperature, battery temperature or the hottest component, chosen in Settings. The Lock Screen and the expanded island show all four together. Thanks to @EASU555 (#6).

Notes:

• Only a running MiniWatts can update or end its Live Activity. Unplug while the app is suspended and the island greys out and the Lock Screen says paused, until you open MiniWatts again or tap End.

Unsigned build — sign it with your own Apple ID before installing. https://github.com/ResistanceTo/MiniWatts#install

新功能:

• 主屏幕与锁屏小组件：显示充电功率和电量。刷新时间由 iOS 决定，通常 15–60 分钟一次，每个小组件都会标明数据的读取时间。.
• 充电实时活动：在锁屏和灵动岛显示充电功率。只在 MiniWatts 运行时更新，App 被挂起后会显示为已暂停。可以在设置里关闭。.
• 悬浮读数：在设置里手动打开的画中画小窗，浮在其他 App 上方，每秒更新一次；开着的时候锁屏也能继续记录充电。会更耗电，用完请关掉。不会播放任何声音。.

修复:

• 部分机型温度读数离谱（比如充电芯片 −9199.4 °C）：物理上不可能的温度现在会被隐藏，不再显示。.

说明:

• 这个版本在 iPhone Air 上开发和验证。传感器的名称和换算因机型而异，其他机型可能有读数不准，欢迎带上机型标识反馈。.
• 小组件会多占用一个 App ID（免费 Apple ID 每周 10 个）。签名工具如果提示移除扩展，移除后就没有小组件了。.

New:

• Home Screen and Lock Screen widget showing charge power and level. iOS decides when it refreshes — usually every 15 to 60 minutes — and each widget shows when its numbers were taken.

Fixed:

• Impossible temperatures on some models (a charge IC at −9199.4 °C) are now hidden instead of shown.

Notes:

• About now says MiniWatts is free and open source, with a link to this repository.
• Built and verified on an iPhone Air. Sensor names and scaling differ between models, so some readings may be wrong on yours — please report them with your model identifier.

Unsigned build — sign it with your own Apple ID before installing. https://github.com/ResistanceTo/MiniWatts#install

Preview 4 repairs controller sleep, disconnect, and reconnect ownership in StarshipPad's existing SDL2/LibUltraShip ControlDeck.

Controller guarantees:

• valid connected controllers keep their existing player port.
• detached or stale handles are closed and cannot occupy a player port.
• a sole returning physical controller reclaims player 1.
• additional physical controllers take the next free port without moving player 1.
• controller ownership changes neutralize buffered buttons, triggers, sticks, and axes.
• reconciliation runs at startup, controller add/remove/remap events, foreground resume, and a bounded one-second active check.
• existing controller preferences and mappings are preserved.

Validation:

The deterministic regression covers missed removal with held input, neutral input after stale ownership release, sole-controller return, additional player 2 assignment, preservation of the unaffected controller, virtual-touch overlap, and foreground reconciliation. Repository safety and the full clean unsigned arm64 iPhoneOS build/package audit passed on GitHub.

A development-signed build 4 was installed in place on a physical iPad under com.chrissotraidis.starshippad. It reached the title/menu, retained the same live PID through background/foreground, and logged foreground controller reconciliation. Pre/post readback hashes matched for the user ROM, generated game archive, Torch hash file, save, touch layout, and Library preferences. The controller config retained all prior values and gained only default secondary-port SDL mappings.

The Simulator sources compiled, but its final link remains blocked by the existing Xcode 26.6 iPhoneOS CoreVideo path mix. No source workaround was added.

Hardware acceptance boundary:

No physical controller was available during this run. Bluetooth reconnect, wired reconnect, natural sleep/wake, full mapping, rumble, touch-overlay transitions with hardware, and two-controller acceptance remain open and are not claimed as passed.

Package status:

StarshipPad-v0.1.0-preview.4-unsigned.ipa is an audited ROM-free, unsigned iPhoneOS arm64 package for self-signing. It is not directly installable as published and is not an App Store or TestFlight build.

apps.localizedDescription:
ByeTunes 🎵:

Say goodbye to iTunes sync!

ByeTunes is a native iOS app that lets you inject music (MP3, M4A, FLAC, WAV) and ringtones directly into your device's media library—without needing a computer connection for every sync. It communicates directly with the iOS media database, giving you the power to manage your music on your terms.

• Metadata Editing: Auto-fetched from iTunes or Deezer.

versions.localizedDescription:
Hi guys, here's the 2.5 update for ByeTunes. This one adds full Deezer support and real parallel downloads for way faster queues, plus a brand new Smart Playlists feature with custom cover art. On top of that, a bunch of reliability fixes across downloads, backups, and repair tools — including a crash fix for the download queue.

Quick recommendation: for the best speed and match accuracy while searching, set Deezer as your Search Provider. And to keep full Apple Music compatibility (animated artwork, richer info), keep Apple Music as your Metadata Source.

Deezer — full provider support.

• Deezer is now a full first-class search source alongside Apple Music/iTunes, with its own tab ("Search or paste a Deezer link").
• Paste a Deezer track/album/artist/playlist link and it resolves directly — same one-tap flow Apple Music/Spotify links already had.
• Deezer artist pages now show real top tracks + full discography (up to 100 each), not just a flat track list.
• Deezer search results paginate ("load more"), merged into the same song/album results as other providers.

Download Engine — real concurrency & speed.

Background Downloads.

• Fixed isAppActive defaulting to true on a silent background relaunch, which routed transfers through the short-lived foreground path instead of the durable background session (caused FLAC→MP3 downgrades and stalls).

• Finished tracks now persist their own .done state so a relaunch mid-queue doesn't drop them from Queue Details.
• Added a genuine background-processing task (registered at launch) so metadata fetching can run even when the app isn't open, instead of only opportunistically while active.
• Each backend candidate now uses its own requested format for its file-extension fallback instead of a hardcoded "flac" default.

• Fixed link.deezer.com short links not resolving.

Smart Playlists.

• Create playlists by rule: Genre, Artist, Decade, Format, or Explicit Rating.
• Multi-select across all rule types with combined naming (e.g. "Rock, Pop" or "1990s, 2000s").
• Live match counts, search within Genre/Artist lists, lossless-format badges.
• Artist grouping splits collab credits ("A & B") into separate artists, matching the on-device Artists tab.
• "Refresh Smart Playlist" — remembers its rule and can re-sync to catch newly matching songs.

Playlists.

• New naming screen matches Apple Music: photo picker, large title field, X/checkmark controls — used for manual and smart playlist creation alike.
• Custom playlist cover photos: pick a photo, it's auto-cropped to a square and uploaded using the same on-device artwork system Apple Music itself uses; persists across relaunch.
• In-playlist rename.
• Playlist restore now lists which specific tracks failed to match instead of just a count.

On-Device Library.

• Select/Select All controls pinned so they stay visible while scrolling.
• Select/Select All/Add to Playlist/Add to Album/Export restricted to the Songs tab; Playlists tab gets Select/Select All/Export/Delete.
• Removed redundant header title/count and Export Folder picker from non-Songs tabs.
• Audio Quality Analysis (new): tapping a song shows a verdict flagging mislabeled files (e.g. an MP3 renamed .flac), suspiciously over-compressed "lossless" files, and low-bitrate lossy files.
• On-device album metadata editing.
• In-place device audio file replacement.
• Content Rating redesigned from a cramped segmented control to a compact menu row, with a new "No Rating" option.
• Fixed the explicit/clean rating editor: a binary toggle could only ever write explicit/none, silently flipping "clean" tracks to explicit.

Reliability Fixes.

• Injection failures no longer silently drop songs from the queue — unconfirmed songs are put back.

• Background metadata fetch no longer double-imports a song if the process is killed mid-drain.
• Artwork upload failures during metadata edits are now reported instead of silently swallowed.
• A failed database integrity check now aborts the library merge instead of writing on top of a known-corrupt database.
• Fixed the large-batch injection safeguard checking the wrong count.
• Fixed a Live Activity race that could resurrect it right after ending; orphaned Live Activities from a killed session now clean up on cold launch.
• Removed dead Tidal/Qobuz code and a broken last-resort Spotify mapping fallback.

Backup & Restore.

• Merged Light/Full Backup toggle and "Export Full Library" into two direct-action rows; Full Backup always bundles per-playlist files.

Settings.

• Store Region picker upgraded from a simple inline row to a full searchable, alphabetically-grouped screen with flags.
• About/Credits moved to its own section, separate from actionable controls.
• Added "Keep Local Metadata" to skip the fetch pipeline for imported local files.

Hi guys, here is the 2.4 update for ByeTunes. This one is focused a lot on making downloads, backups, playlists and repair tools way more reliable and easier to use.

Downloads can now keep going in the background. If you turn on background downloads in Settings, ByeTunes can continue an active download after you leave the app or lock your phone instead of making you babysit the download screen.

There is also Live Activity support now. When background downloads are enabled you can turn on Live Activity Progress and see the current download progress on the Lock Screen and Dynamic Island.

Metadata fetching for downloaded songs was improved too. ByeTunes can now keep track of downloaded files that still need metadata and finish that work in the background, so songs downloaded from the Download tab should still get cleaned up and enriched even if you do not manually open the Music tab right away.

Small disclaimer for background downloads:

If you manually force close the app from the app switcher, iOS may stop background activity until you open ByeTunes again.

Opus support was added too. ByeTunes can now detect and handle Opus downloads properly instead of treating them like an unknown audio file type, so downloads that come back as Opus should be saved and processed with the right extension.

The download queue is more persistent now. If the app closes or gets interrupted, ByeTunes saves the active queue, failed items, progress state and pending metadata work so it can recover better next time. Failed Apple Music downloads also give a clearer message now, and there is a helper to find the song on Spotify when Apple Music cannot be used for that track.

I also cleaned up the Download tab search bar. You can now use the same bar to search or paste an Apple Music, Spotify or Deezer link instead of having to think so much about where the link came from.

Backup and Restore got a big rework. There is now a dedicated Backup & Restore section with a cleaner Manage Backups screen. You can still do light database backups or full backups with song files.

Playlist backup and restore was added too. You can back up playlists using a 3mu file on your device, then restore them later, or even share them with your friends. ByeTunes tries to match the songs already on the device when restoring, so playlists can be recreated without needing to re-inject every song again.

The On-Device Library browser got a lot better. You can now browse songs, artists, albums and playlists, manage playlists from inside ByeTunes, add songs to playlists, remove songs from playlists, rename/delete playlists and export songs with a saved export folder.

The repair tools were moved into a proper Library Repair area. Clean & Repair Library is now separated from Backup & Restore, and there are clearer tools for fixing ghost songs, broken alphabetical ordering, artwork issues and album artwork refreshes.

There were also a bunch of smaller fixes and cleanups around metadata, backups, device library browsing, download recovery, queue handling and settings organization.

Thanks as always to everyone testing ByeTunes, sending logs and reporting what breaks. Hope you guys enjoy this update.

Hi guys, here is the 2.3 update for ByeTunes. I know its been quite sometime since the last update but i was finally able to get my hands to work again. A good amount of things got added, fixed and improved in this one.

From now on I am hosting our own server so we don't rely on external servers anymore, I am solely assuming the cost of this server myself however if anybody is willing to support us there is a new option to support us inside the settings tab. Whoever does will be featured in the settings tab.

You can now also search and download from Spotify directly. Spotify has been added as a search provider in the Download tab right next to Apple Music. You can paste a Spotify link or search by name and it works the same way as everything else.

Downloads now have a Pause and a Cancel button while a download is in progress. You can pause a download mid-flight and resume it, or cancel it without having to clear the entire queue.

The output format setting was broken. If you had FLAC selected, downloads would sometimes come in as MP3 anyway. That was a bug where the format preference was not being read correctly when using the auto backend path. That is fixed now and the format you pick in settings is what you actually get.

There is a new On-Device Library section in Settings. It lets you browse all the songs currently injected on your connected device. From there you can edit metadata, delete songs, and export files. It is disabled and grayed out when no device local tunnel vpn is connected.

When you are manually editing a song's metadata, there is now a Custom Album Color option. If you turn it on, a color picker shows up and you can pick any color you want for the album background inside the music app.

On the fixes side, there was a crash that could happen in the download backend when a custom download handler was used instead of a URL request. That is fixed. The metadata parser had a bug where if a filename contained "feat." in the title, the heuristic would swap the title and artist around. That is also fixed.

Thanks as always to everyone testing and sending logs. Hope you enjoy this one.

apps.localizedDescription:
LetsFLUTssh:

Disclaimer: This is a functional neuroslop pet project — built with AI assistance under the supervision and direction of a real developer, for personal use, self-education, and fun. Use at your own risk.

Cross-platform SSH/SFTP client with GUI — Flutter UI on a Rust core (security, transport, terminal emulation via alacritty_terminal, and SQLCipher all inside lfs_core + lfs_os_security, bridged via flutter_rust_bridge; Flutter only renders, secrets never cross to Dart). What it is:

Tsumiru is a Flutter client for Suwayomi-Server, the self-hosted manga server. You point it at a server you already run. Tsumiru itself is only the reader (the server handles sources and downloads).

Runs on Android, Linux, Windows, macOS, and Web.

apps.subtitle: Native iOS build of the Gen 1 recomp engine, with optional 3D voxel rendering. Bring your own ROM
apps.localizedDescription:
VoxelTrail for iOS:

Español · English.

A native iOS build of the Gen 1 recomp engine — the Generation 1 Pokémon games, reimplemented in Lua on LÖVE — with the Dramatic Shape voxel mod built in, so the overworld can be played as a 3D diorama or in first person.

You need your own ROM. None is included here and none will be. The app reads a Game Boy ROM you already own and extracts its data on first launch.

Install:

The IPA is unsigned, which is what sideloading tools expect — they sign it with your own Apple ID, on your own device.

• Install a sideloader. SideStore or AltStore. Follow their setup; both need a one-time pairing step with a computer.

versions.localizedDescription:
Unsigned IPA — install with SideStore or AltStore. Requires iOS 16+, tested on iOS 26.6. Bring your own ROM.

📖 Instrucciones en español · 🇪🇸 Notas en español abajo.

Pokémon Stadium battle models:

3D BATTLES can fight with the Pokémon Stadium models instead of the flat Game Boy pictures — STADIUM A on the map, STADIUM B on two discs against the sky.

You supply the cartridge. Import Stadium ROM in the launcher's MODS panel, or STADIUM ROM in the options menu, opens the Files picker for your Pokémon Stadium (US) 1.0 file. The models are built on your device, once, and the ROM is read and forgotten rather than kept.

That picker is new work on my side: iOS had no way to hand the mod a cartridge at all, so it printed a sandbox path and asked you to put a file somewhere a phone cannot reach. Now upstream as.

US 1.0 specifically — every model offset is measured against that revision. Another one builds, and the screen tells you the models may be wrong.

The battle HUD reads the right way round:

1.7.2 draws the battle HUD mirrored on iOS — PIKACHU, the HP numbers and L100 all backwards, while FIGHT/ITEM/RUN reads fine. It comes from a fix that assumes iOS presents the HUD canvas upside down and corrects for it; this build's renderer doesn't flip it, so the correction was the mirror. Fixed, and the frosted panels behind the HUD come back with it.

More of the mod:

• RENDER DIST — FIT / WIDE / WIDER / WIDEST / OFF. The first thing to reach for if 3D runs slowly: FIT skips whole connected maps before they cost anything.
• Fog and god rays in Viridian Forest, every battle location rebuilt, and a lot of new voxel work — diner stools, mansion desks, CUT trees.
• ROUND WORLD gained two rungs, GLOBE and PLANET. PLANET is a true half-sphere: the town sitting on a little world.

Spanish:

The Stadium screens and the whole STADIUM ROM flow are translated. Two older gaps closed: CANCEL was the one English word left on a fully Spanish options menu — structurally unreachable, now fixed and — and ten strings carried Ñ, ¿ or ¡ onto the 8×8 font, which has no glyph for any of them and drew holes instead.

The translation is.

Kept from before:

The live-tuning panel, the look stick, readable setting names, third person, the battle camera, and Spanish Red/Blue ROM support.

🇪🇸 En español:

IPA sin firmar — instalalo con SideStore o AltStore. Requiere iOS 16 o posterior; probado en iOS 26.6. Necesitas tu propia ROM.

📖 Instrucciones completas en español.

Modelos de combate de Pokemon Stadium:

COMBATES 3D puede pelear con los modelos de Pokemon Stadium en vez de con las imagenes planas de Game Boy: STADIUM A sobre el mapa, STADIUM B sobre dos discos contra el cielo.

El cartucho lo pones tu. Importar ROM de Stadium, en el panel de MODS del menu inicial, o ROM STADIUM en las opciones, abre el selector de Archivos para tu Pokemon Stadium (US) 1.0. Los modelos se crean en tu dispositivo una sola vez, y la ROM se lee y se olvida en lugar de guardarse.

Ese selector es trabajo nuevo de mi parte: en iOS no habia forma de entregarle un cartucho al mod, asi que imprimia una ruta interna y te pedia dejar un archivo en un sitio al que un telefono no llega.

US 1.0 en concreto: cada medida de los modelos esta tomada de esa revision. Otra distinta se construye igual, pero la pantalla te avisa de que pueden salir mal.

El HUD de combate se lee del derecho:

La 1.7.2 dibuja el HUD de combate reflejado en iOS: PIKACHU, los numeros de PS y L100 al reves, mientras que LUCHA/OBJETO/HUIR se lee bien. Viene de un arreglo que da por hecho que iOS presenta ese lienzo del reves y lo corrige; el motor de esta version no lo voltea, asi que la correccion era el reflejo. Arreglado, y los paneles esmerilados de detras del HUD vuelven con ello.

Mas del mod:

• DISTANCIA — AJUSTE / LEJOS / MAS LEJOS / MAXIMO / NO. Lo primero que tocar si el 3D va lento: AJUSTE descarta mapas enteros antes de que cuesten nada.
• Niebla y rayos de sol en el Bosque Verde, todas las localizaciones de combate rehechas, y mucho trabajo nuevo de voxeles.
• MUNDO CURVO gano dos niveles, GLOBO y PLANETA. PLANETA es media esfera de verdad: el pueblo sobre un planeta pequeño.

Español:

Las pantallas de Stadium y todo el proceso de ROM STADIUM estan traducidos. Se cierran dos huecos antiguos: CANCELAR era la unica palabra en ingles que quedaba en un menu de opciones completamente en español, y diez textos llevaban Ñ, ¿ o ¡ a la fuente de 8x8, que no tiene glifo para ninguno y dibujaba huecos.

Se mantiene todo lo anterior:

El panel de ajuste en vivo, la palanca de vista, los nombres legibles de los ajustes, la tercera persona, la camara de combate y el soporte de ROMs de Rojo y Azul en español.

Unsigned IPA — install with SideStore or AltStore. Requires iOS 16+, tested on iOS 26.6. Bring your own ROM.

📖 Instrucciones en español.

Bundles Dramatic Shape v1.5.5, up from 1.5.4.

3D WORLD → 3RD PERSON now uses DramaticShape's boom camera, which replaces the simpler one I had written. It is better where mine was weakest:

• It does not clip through walls. The boom marches back through the terrain and the map's walkability, so backing into a corner walks the camera toward your shoulders rather than through the geometry — and eases back out once the corner clears, rather than snapping.
• A shoulder offset keeps your character off dead centre.
• The boom eases between first and third person instead of cutting.
• Your character turns along a continuous bearing as he walks, not four fixed directions.

Pinch sets the distance — no menu rows for it any more.

Battle camera:

Drag or use the right stick during a battle to walk the camera around the arena, and pinch to work its lens. The fight is staged on the map itself, so there is a real scene to look around.

Kept from before:

Everything: the live-tuning panel, Spanish throughout, the on-screen look stick and its rows, readable setting names, and Spanish Red/Blue ROM support.

Note:

3RD (EXPERIMENTAL) is shown as 3RD PERSON here — 18 characters is drawn off the edge of a 160px screen, the same issue reported upstream for the first-person rung.

🇪🇸 En español:

IPA sin firmar — instalalo con SideStore o AltStore. Requiere iOS 16 o posterior; probado en iOS 26.6. Necesitas tu propia ROM.

📖 Instrucciones completas en español.

Incluye Dramatic Shape v1.5.5, actualizado desde la 1.5.4.

MUNDO 3D → 3A PERSONA usa ahora la camara con brazo de DramaticShape, que sustituye a la mas sencilla que habia escrito yo. Es mejor justo donde la mia flojeaba:

• No atraviesa las paredes. El brazo recorre el terreno y las zonas transitables del mapa, asi que si retrocedes a un rincon la camara se acerca a tus hombros en vez de meterse en la geometria, y vuelve a salir cuando se despeja.
• Un desplazamiento lateral deja al personaje fuera del centro exacto.
• El brazo hace una transicion suave entre primera y tercera persona.
• Tu personaje gira con un rumbo continuo al andar, no con cuatro direcciones fijas.

Pellizca para ajustar la distancia: ya no hay filas de menu para eso.

Camara en los combates:

Arrastra o usa el stick derecho durante un combate para mover la camara por el escenario, y pellizca para ajustar el objetivo. El combate se juega sobre el propio mapa, asi que hay una escena real que mirar.

Se mantiene todo lo anterior:

El panel de ajuste en vivo, el español en toda la app, la palanca de vista y sus filas, los nombres legibles de los ajustes, y el soporte de ROMs de Rojo y Azul en español.

Unsigned IPA — install with SideStore or AltStore. Requires iOS 16+, tested on iOS 26.6. Bring your own ROM.

📖 Instrucciones en español.

Bundles Dramatic Shape v1.5.4, the version everything here was tested against.

Third person:

3D WORLD → 3RD PERSON — a chase camera behind your character. He turns to face where he walks, the camera swings low when you look down, and DISTANCE and CAM HEIGHT let you frame it. Both are in the live-tuning panel, so you can set them while watching.

Spanish, properly:

The whole app now — launcher, game cards, save slots, mod browser, options. Set your phone to Spanish and it opens that way; otherwise the button beside Touch Controls switches it.

And Spanish Red and Blue ROMs work, via by jherediagu — Edición Roja and Edición Azul play in Spanish, sharing a tab and saves with the US versions. Spanish Yellow can't be supported; no disassembly exists for it.

Also:

• New app icon.
• Fixed: the live-tuning panel had no rows and did nothing when switched on.
• Fixed: a crash on launch in 0.2.0.

Known limits:

• The chase camera can clip through walls if you back into a corner at a long DISTANCE.
• FIT, SLOW, MEDIUM and FAST stay English — they are raw literals in the engine, not reachable by any translation.

IPA sin firmar — instalalo con SideStore o AltStore. Requiere iOS 16 o posterior; probado en iOS 26.6. Necesitas tu propia ROM.

versions.localizedDescription:
Release v1.1.6:

• Fixed resumed manga panels not rendering until user scroll action — root cause was a desynchronization between currentPage, scrolledID, and sliderValue when restoring reading progress, which caused isAllowedToLoad to deadlock on unmounted offscreen pages.
• Fixed scrubber slider staying at page 1 on resume — slider value now initializes to the resumed page and stays synced with scroll position during normal reading.
• Improved Analytics chart scaling across long time ranges — replaced Catmull-Rom interpolation with monotone cubic to prevent negative read dips, added proper calendar units to bar marks, and implemented adaptive day/month/year bucketing for multi-year data.
• Removed dead Cache Expiry setting that was never wired to Nuke's disk cache eviction.
• Fixed inflated cache size reporting — now shows actual disk cache usage only, excluding volatile in-memory bitmap overhead.
• Stopped aggressive RAM cache purging on reader exit that was clearing all cached thumbnails app-wide.
• Cache size changes no longer rebuild the entire image pipeline — updates the existing DataCache.sizeLimit directly.

Release v1.1.5.

• Added Database Sync options in Settings > Server with automated sync status polling and delayed confirmations on potentially destructive actions.

• Updated Analytics view to dynamically bucket data by days, months, or years depending on the time scale.
• Replaced line charts with bar charts for long-term analytics data to improve readability.
• Added a toggle under Network settings to automatically hide suspected broken manga listings from UI grids.
• Updated UI iconography for improved theme support.

Known possible bugs -.

• Cache limits not being adhered to always.
• Analytics (depending on the usage timeframe).
• When resuming a previously read manga, panels don't load until user scroll action.

• v1.1.2: Improved thumbnail fallbacks even more.
• v1.1.3: Normalize HTML entities in titles and format .NET ticks into readable dates.
• v1.1.4: Fix missing zero in .NET ticks offset causing the wrong year to be shown.

apps.name: Kryptos
apps.subtitle: Encrypt right inside any messenger: the keyboard encrypts, the screen decrypts, no jumping between apps. iOS and Android, Signal Protocol, fully offline
apps.localizedDescription:
Kryptos:

Kryptos is an iPhone and Android app that encrypts conversations inside any messenger.

You type the message straight into WhatsApp, Telegram or an SMS, tap the padlock on the Kryptos keyboard, and the field holds ciphertext instead of your text. On the other end it works the other way round: on Android Kryptos decrypts the text on screen without leaving the messenger, on iPhone it shows the text above the keyboard once the ciphertext is copied. The messenger, the carrier and anyone who intercepts the message on the way see a run of characters they cannot read.

The app is the same on both systems and uses one format, so it does not matter which phone your contact carries.

versions.localizedDescription:
New features:

• Persian language.
• Automatic clipboard clearing is now 1 minute by default.
• The encryption icon on the keyboard has been changed when “Send after encryption” mode is enabled.
• When screen recording or broadcasting, Kryptos hides the conversation and shows a placeholder.
• Before sending decrypted text to another app, Kryptos now asks for confirmation.
• Encryption buttons are disabled in password input fields.
• When decryption is disabled on screen, the service itself is now also disabled; previously, it continued running in the background.
• Voice input has been added to the keyboard.

• When scrolling up through the conversation, a button to return to the latest message appears.
• Text from Kryptos screens is no longer passed to Android system suggestions.
• “How to use” on the conversation screens is now a link.
• On Android, a “Do not pause the app” option has been added under “Privacy - On screen”.
• Keyboards have been adjusted to the system size. Larger letters, taller keys, wider spacing.
• Double-tapping the period on the keyboard inserts a comma (disabled by default). This can be changed in the keyboard settings in the app.
• App lock has been redesigned.

Bug fixes:

• If you switch to another app immediately after pressing “Encrypt”, the text is no longer inserted into it.
• The public key is no longer automatically removed from the clipboard.
• Large photos no longer cause the app to close when extracting a message from them.
• A message decrypted by the keyboard no longer disappears from the conversation.
• App lock immediately revokes the keyboard’s access to encryption; previously, access remained for several more minutes.
• The delay after entering an incorrect code can no longer be reset by restarting the app.
• Automatic clipboard clearing no longer deletes data copied in other apps.
• The “Copy” button in the on-screen decryption panel now correctly copies the text.
• The keyboard no longer suggests or remembers words in fields for secret phrases and one-time codes.
• The keyboard no longer reports that steganography is unavailable if the message was actually hidden.
• Turning the clock back no longer allows decrypted text to remain in memory longer than intended.
• On-screen decryption no longer lags on screens with a large amount of text.
• Interrupted panic wipe no longer leaves the app on the recovery screen.
• A deleted PGP key no longer reappears after restarting the app.
• The keyboard no longer lags in long conversations.
• When launching Kryptos, it no longer contacts Google services to load the emoji font.
• The emoji panel opens correctly again after switching between light and dark themes.
• Re-adding a contact with the same saved key no longer permanently breaks the conversation in one direction.
• When decryption fails, the app now states the reason if the key has already been used or has expired, instead of displaying a message about an incorrect contact.
• An error in a background task no longer crashes the app together with the keyboard.
• Other fixes.

Downloads:

The APK is built in the F-Droid buildserver container and signed with the same key as before, so it installs over an existing copy. The IPA is unsigned.

What is new:

• Chinese: the interface and a keyboard layout with pinyin input.
• Profanity, insults and potentially dangerous words are out of all three text steganography modes, in English, Russian and German. 197 words were replaced with neutral ones, so each language still holds 4,096 words.
• Keyboard: the Paste and Clear buttons are bigger and sit in one row, the message field size is adjustable, and the Kryptos badge can be hidden.
• Send after encrypting now works in messengers that send with their own button. It needs the on-screen decryption service, which Android switches off on update.
• Profiles and contacts can be renamed, a long press on a message opens a menu with copy and delete, and a deleted message is wiped completely.
• A profile with unreadable storage no longer takes the app down: it opens on a working profile and names the one that is unavailable.

Fixes:

Around twenty, among them: send after encrypting did not send in messengers with their own button, the keyboard closed after sending, switching to a profile with damaged storage closed the app and left it on the erase-everything screen, the app could create a key over existing data and make it unreadable, the password stayed in memory after the key was derived, hiding a message in a photo used 80 MB more memory than needed.

Breaking change. Covers made by the ordinary-words and smart-sentences steganography modes cannot be read by versions before 2.3.2. Both sides have to update.

Changelog - Kryptos 2.3.1:

New.

• The app is fully translated into German.
• Keyboard: a QWERTZ layout with ä ö ü ß and its own dictionaries (40,000 frequent words, 177,000 word forms, 640 bigrams), with suggestions and autocorrect at the same level as Russian and English. Nouns are suggested capitalised, the case taken from a corpus that preserves it.
• Steganography in all three modes: a 4,096-word list, "smart sentence" grammar with German word order and cases, and the random-letter mode.
• The suggestion engine went from two languages to an arbitrary number.
• The keyboard declares three layouts in the system input-language switcher, and picking one there switches the layout inside the keyboard.
• Length masking now works in steganography too, in all three modes and all languages. Before this the switch did nothing once steganography was on, and the length of the text could be read straight off the length of the cover.
• A new keyboard mode on Android: the padlock encrypts the message and sends it in the messenger right away, and a paper-plane badge appears on the padlock. Off by default, switched on in Settings -> Keyboard.
• Other changes.

Fixed.

• Confirmation popups ("Erase all" and ten more dialogs) no longer appear off to one side, they are anchored to the button that opened them.
• On-screen stego decryption: a sender name that matched a dictionary word (Weber, Richter, Koch) broke parsing and the message would not decrypt. A second bug: a stray word at the end of the node (a timestamp, "Heute") threw away a message that had already been parsed. Added limited resynchronisation and anchoring on the sentence boundary. Affects every language, not only German.
• The key preview was not covered by the screenshot block and showed even in password fields: on a screen recording of a "protected" keyboard the typed text could be read character by character.
• An oversized photo or an oversized backup file crashed the app out of memory instead of returning a clear error.
• The app stalled on launch once every two days, which is when the Signal keys were being rotated.
• Opening the app with a long text in the clipboard made the interface lag.
• Holding backspace with two fingers did not stop the deletion.
• Switching a PGP key and deleting a recipient froze the screen.
• The illustrated guide loaded every image at once, now they load as you scroll.
• The keyboard held twice the memory it needed while loading dictionaries.
• After a profile switch the keyboard showed the decryption from the previous profile.
• A corrupted backup file wiped the working PGP keys instead of being rejected.
• Length masking ate up to half the capacity of a photo while hiding nothing: the size of the shot does not depend on the length of the message. It has been removed from photos.
• App launch waited for the whole message history to be parsed.
• The message history was re-encrypted and written again on every launch, even when nothing had changed.
• Picking a photo decoded the whole shot just for a thumbnail, and hiding and extracting ran on the main thread.
• Key export and import and PGP operations froze with no progress indicator.
• Regenerating a PGP key took the algorithm from the new-key form.
• Deleting a PGP recipient happened without confirmation.
• The pressed-key highlight disappeared from under the finger after the very first letter.
• A message you had already read stopped opening again after the next 64 arrived.
• The wording about being offline in the help was made precise: the app opens no network connections.
• The green clipboard dot on the decrypt button in the keyboard could swallow the tap instead of the button.
• Other changes.

IMPORTANT: the stego format has changed. Messages with length masking on will not open in older builds.
