versions.localizedDescription:
0.4.0 Beta 15 - Episode handoffs, paused Dolby Vision, and playback recovery:

Install this over any earlier Apple build. Beta 15 brings together the Apple playback work tested in local builds 248–250, plus a new guard for next episodes starting several seconds into the video. Apple build 251. All Beta 14 changes are retained; no earlier executable or release package has been substituted.

This is an Apple-only update for Apple TV, iPhone, iPad, and Apple Silicon Mac. Android remains on the signed Beta 14 packages described below.

What's fixed:

Next episodes no longer accept an unexpected multi-second opening as a normal start. A device diagnostic showed a fresh episode committing at 4.046 seconds despite a zero resume point and auto-skip being off. The new check intercepts that first position before it can update the episode identity or watch progress, and makes one precise return to the opening on the already-running player. It does not restart the stream or change your pause state. Genuine resume points, live streams, and your own seeks stay in charge. If the correction cannot reach the opening, the app reports a source failure instead of quietly skipping ahead or repeatedly rewinding. This targets the observed next-episode handoff; the separate native decoder failure still needs device verification.

Next-episode preloading can retain the whole requested warm prefix. The preloader requested the first 32 MiB but its response-size validator could reject that same valid response. The limit now matches the request. This removes a specific reason prepared streams were discarded and had to start cold; it is not a promise that every Usenet source can prepare instantly on every server.

Changing or recovering a source no longer introduces its own hidden Pause. An implementation pause used while rejecting or retiring a source could survive an in-place player replacement, leaving the new source frozen despite having data. That synthetic pause is removed. An actual viewer pause is still preserved, but is bound only after the replacement is accepted. A failed retiring engine's paused flag does not get mistaken for your choice. Rejected replacements retain the current load's state.

A paused Dolby Vision stream can recover an expired local HLS playlist without skipping the episode or immediately falling back. The device trace identified a real conflict: while paused, the bounded local producer stopped adding segments, and AVFoundation eventually rejected the unchanged growing playlist. One failure callback previously bypassed the existing paused-recovery path. It now keeps same-mount recovery evidence and waits for Play. Duplicate failure callbacks coalesce, and existing position, track-selection and DV restoration stay attached to the current item. No fake segments or unbounded producer buffer have been added.

A producer finishing while you are paused does not mean you finished watching. Recovery now distinguishes the producer's final playlist from the viewer's actual position. A retained position inside that finished playlist can resume; a real end remains an end, and an invalid or evicted position remains a source error. Retry budgets only re-arm after sustained real playback, not seek jumps or paused ticks, preventing repeated item-replacement loops.

A stream ending early cannot casually mark the episode watched and play the next one. Both Apple playback surfaces now compare a decoder's EOF against load-owned position and known duration. An EOF far before the ending enters same-episode source recovery instead of completion handling. Recovery uses observed playback position, not an optimistic scrub target or old resume floor. Duplicate EOF callbacks cannot spend the recovery budget twice. True endings, live playback, trailers and unknown-duration sources keep their existing semantics. This addresses the premature-completion code gap examined alongside issue #223.

Replacement items do not inherit the previous item's completion evidence. AVPlayer can recover a physical item while retaining the logical playback request. Completion evidence now also follows the physical item generation, so an old early-EOF rejection cannot prevent the recovered item from genuinely finishing later. Retired callbacks cannot finish a newer episode.

Apple TV's short backward/forward seeks receive the same refill protection as a scrub. A relative seek outside the buffered window previously missed the existing refill hold and bounded recovery watchdog. It now uses that protection while retaining relative seek semantics and your latest Pause/Play choice. In-buffer seeks do not unnecessarily invoke the cold-refill path.

Continue Watching keeps the episode you actually opened when it needs to show Details. Local CW navigation on Apple TV and iPhone now carries the exact episode ID and resume point into the detail page. An episode with a zero resume point is still a valid selection; it does not fall back to an unwatched special such as S0E1. After you successfully play a newer episode, that newer local receipt supersedes the older navigation hint. If a partial episode list does not yet contain the exact target, the hero waits rather than inventing a different episode.

The phone's resume offset must belong to its selected episode. The detail hero no longer applies an offset from one episode to a different selected episode. This matches the existing episode-identity check on Apple TV.

Up from the first episode returns to the selected season. On Apple TV, that move now explicitly reveals and focuses the current season chip instead of jumping to the hero or making you navigate back down from Play. Down from the first episode still moves to the second; deeper episode rows retain their normal navigation.

Supported native AVPlayer WebVTT subtitles can follow the in-player appearance settings. Their timed text can now use the existing VortX subtitle overlay, so outline, shaded and box styles are app-controlled. The native renderer is suppressed before supported text is displayed, and cues replace rather than accumulate. Seeks, subtitle changes, item replacements and close clear or fence stale cues. Unsupported or bitmap captions remain native; Picture in Picture and AirPlay retain native captions. This does not change the device's system caption settings or claim styling support for every subtitle format.

Diagnostics preserve useful decoder failure reasons without exporting raw decoder traffic. Probe-enabled release builds now retain bounded, allowlisted VideoToolbox failure categories, including bad frame status, no-output callbacks, session/format failure and waiting for a keyframe. Signed stream links, request headers and arbitrary log text are excluded. This helps distinguish a native decoding failure from an output-frame drop or an empty network cache.

Android:

The separately recorded Android rapid-title-selection race and Android update-feed correction remain open. Use the matching Beta 14 APK directly while that feed still serves the older entry.

Verification and remaining limits:

The fresh-origin recovery was also exercised against the exact bundled GPL playback libraries with VideoToolbox, GPU-next/MoltenVK and AVFoundation audio. A controlled 4.046-second initial position returned to zero while playing and while paused, without changing the pause state. The matching source itself contains timestamps starting at zero.

These are specific repairs, not a claim that every playback problem is solved. The physical Apple TV's initial hardware-decoder failure has not been reproduced on the Mac, and broader active-play DV stalls, provider-specific buffering and sustained NNTP throughput still need live-device testing. This release does not force software decoding, remove Dolby Vision, or disguise a failed source as a completed episode. The broader Android parity and phone/Mac redesign work is not bundled into this playback cut.

Please test:

• Let a series advance automatically and use the next-episode button. Confirm the opening is shown, the selected episode is correct, and watch progress belongs to that episode.
• Pause a DV/AVPlayer title long enough for the local producer to stop filling, then resume. Confirm it stays paused until Play and recovers the same episode and selections.
• Seek backward and forward both inside and outside the buffered window, including while paused.
• Open Family Guy or another series from CW. If Details opens, confirm it targets the current episode instead of an unwatched special. From the first episode, press Up once to reach the season selector.
• With supported built-in AVPlayer text subtitles, compare outline and box appearance. Include the subtitle format and a diagnostic if it remains native or ignores styling.

Install:

Apple TV. Use VortX-tvOS-v0.4.0-beta.15-ci.ipa for Full or VortX-tvOS-lite-v0.4.0-beta.15-ci.ipa for Lite. Install the same variant you normally use through your signing service.

Check SHA256SUMS-ci.txt; the immutable tag, source commit, and protected release workflow provide provenance for the published Apple files. This beta is deliberately promoted to Latest; Apple update and install feeds are verified as part of publication.

0.4.0 Beta 14 - Paused playback, episode artwork, and Android fixes:

Install this over any earlier build. Beta 14 adds another focused round of Apple playback repairs, fixes stale and missing episode artwork, makes the phone's source controls readable, and brings Android fixes into the same release. Apple build 247; Android version code 237. All Beta 12 changes are retained; its already-published packages and tag have not been replaced.

Beta 13 remained an unpublished draft. This release bundles its completed work with the final reviewed profile, Discover, and Android title-relation changes, all built from the same new source revision.

What's fixed on Apple:

Returning to the app no longer reconnects a deliberately paused video. Foreground recovery previously treated a playhead that had not moved during a pause as a reason to refresh a debrid link or remount a local server connection. A delayed local-server check could do the same after a pause. Those checks now wait for Play, retain the suspension context, and belong to the exact current load. Changing source, episode, or player retires the old request. Real connection recovery remains available when you resume; this does not simply disable the recovery path. Apple TV, iPhone, and iPad.

A fresh-link response respects the latest Pause or Play press. On iPhone, iPad, and Mac, a debrid refresh remembered the transport state from before its network request. Pausing while that request was running could therefore start the replacement playing. The accepted replacement now explicitly applies your current intent, whether paused or playing. Apple TV retains its existing load-bound transport handoff.

A failed native player initialization reports an error instead of exiting the app. Allocation or initialization failure now reaches the current playback error path. A late failure from a retired load cannot appear on a newer title. This repairs a concrete process-exit path; it is not a claim that every reported launch crash has the same cause.

Episode artwork and metadata can recover after the first response. Episode heroes and thumbnails try the episode image, series background, and poster in order, without retrying the same failed candidate indefinitely. A late image result cannot overwrite a newer request. Apple TV's cached episode rows now refresh when the actual episode metadata changes, not only when the episode count changes. That also fixes same-count corrections to titles and season membership. Series watched rollups and season validity refresh on metadata changes across Apple platforms, while a valid manual season selection remains selected. Spoiler protection is retained.

The phone hero is taller, and the source controls no longer squeeze into vertical text. Portrait phone detail heroes use approximately 78% of the viewport. Play has its own row; Quality, Player, and Audio wrap below it at readable sizes. Tablet and landscape sizing remain separate. This is a targeted layout repair, not a claim that the entire planned phone or Mac redesign is finished.

Normal source rows preserve the add-on's formatting. Authored names and descriptions retain their line breaks, Unicode, emoji, and spacing instead of being replaced by a truncated parsed filename. Missing descriptions still have a filename fallback. The optional compact presentation remains compact.

Android:

Android returns after the Apple-only betas. The Android packages also include the retained work since the last public Android build, Beta 1. Both APK variants contain phone and Android TV interfaces; "Full/MPV" and "Play/Media3" describe the player/distribution variant, not separate phone and TV apps.

Progressive native Usenet playback and safer cancellation. The retained Android NZB/NNTP work adds progressive playback, bounded parsing and assembly, credential ownership, and cleanup of cancelled or superseded playback leases. Back or a source change cannot let a late fetch revive the abandoned session. The cancellation regression now tests a genuinely stalled HTTP response body. Live-provider speed and device-specific buffering still require testing.

Source handoffs and split audio are better coordinated. Resolver results are fenced to the current playback request, source and player switches cannot accept obsolete completions, and MPV teardown drops retired failure callbacks. Split audio is configured before the new video load, avoiding an audio command racing against the outgoing item. Audio-health checks re-arm when a valid track list arrives.

MPV teardown no longer mutates a live observer list during dispatch. Observer callbacks use a stable snapshot, so a callback that removes an observer during close or recovery cannot invalidate that iteration. Callbacks run outside the registry lock.

Unavailable audio metadata is not mistaken for a video with no audio. Null, malformed, and incomplete track snapshots retain the last valid state. A genuinely empty track list is handled separately. The final audio-health check no longer cancels itself while refreshing metadata, so the existing recovery path can act on an unavailable or failed audio output.

Failed-source controls are reachable with a TV remote. Focus moves to a usable source or the close control after source results or failure. Focused controls have a visible border, and Cancel stays available while a replacement is resolving. Back and cancellation retain their existing request-ownership checks.

Source details remain readable on narrower screens. Badges wrap instead of competing for one oversized row. Phone and TV source rows keep the add-on's authored description and line breaks; the optional compact phone view remains parsed and short.

Missing primary artwork has a fallback. Phone heroes and episode images, plus TV detail backdrops, can fall back to other available artwork. Failed or outdated image callbacks cannot advance a newer request. TV's background gradient and episode spoiler blur remain in place.

Plex manual linking requests a compatible short code. The Android manual-link flow now requests the code type expected by plex.tv/link, matching the existing Apple flow.

The retained interface and profile work is included too. Android gains the rotating phone Home hero, TV ambient-hero lifecycle repair and poster-style preferences, source-scoped player selection, detail-source audio selection, and debrid-cloud access from Search. Discovery settings are profile-scoped, overlay watched mutations retain their recency, and the TV scrubber and player controls have explicit remote-focus handling. These are incremental parity improvements, not a finished one-to-one Apple redesign.

Declared prequels and sequels are reachable on phone and TV. Supported add-on relation links open internal movie or series detail pages, including namespaced anime IDs carried by supported series routes. Invalid links, unsupported types, self-links, and duplicate entries are skipped. This does not infer a chronology or add support for every custom add-on media type.

Movie collections offer dated release neighbors. Previous and next titles use valid release dates and the exact current collection member. These are explicitly labeled release order, not narrative prequels or sequels; undated titles remain available in the full collection.

Discover's collections setting now controls Discover. TV previously read the Home visibility switch, and phone Discover had no collections-hub consumer. Both now use an independent Discover model, load artwork, react to provider and region changes, and cancel obsolete refresh work. A regression test also covers a settings notification arriving during initial loading, before the previous implementation had subscribed.

Profiles:

Collections visibility stays with the selected profile on Apple and Android. Home and Discover visibility now travel in the profile's discovery preferences instead of leaking through global settings. Partial sync documents retain existing choices; switching to a profile without a saved value uses the default. Apple views and the open Android settings screen refresh when the active profile changes.

Updates and install feeds:

Latest beta publication and update feeds now agree. The authenticated feed receiver accepts the release coordinator's explicitly selected Latest-beta channel while retaining its signature, asset, source, checksum, and generation checks. Publication proves the release became public before requesting Latest, and records that exact publication immediately so a failed Latest step can compensate the correct release. Ordinary prereleases still do not take over Latest. Beta 12's public feeds were separately repaired and verified; this build retains those fixes.

Verification and remaining limits:

Physical playback still matters. These are specific implemented repairs, not a blanket promise of zero DV stalls, zero dropped frames, or flawless live NNTP throughput on every device and provider. Full Apple-to-Android feature/design parity and the broader phone/Mac redesign remain ongoing work. A separately identified Android rapid-title-selection race is recorded for the next work session; it was not bundled as an untested last-minute change.

Please test:

• Pause an Apple TV video, leave the app, return, and confirm it stays paused. Then press Play and confirm a moved local-server connection or stale provider link can recover without selecting the episode again.
• Pause or resume while a debrid source is reconnecting on iPhone or Mac; the replacement should follow your latest choice.
• Open an anime or series whose episode artwork arrives late. Images and corrected episode metadata should update without changing seasons first.
• On iPhone, check the larger hero, the Play row and filters, and your add-on's original multi-line source descriptions.
• On Android TV, test HTTP add-ons, MPV audio, repeated source refresh, failure recovery, and closing the player using only the remote. Report remaining failures with a diagnostic log and the selected player.

Install:

Android update-check limitation: the new signed Beta 14 APKs are published below, but the Android in-app update feed is still serving the earlier Beta 1 entry. Install the matching APK directly from this release for now. Apple appcast and install feeds have been verified on Beta 14. The Android feed correction remains separate work; the release APKs have not been relabeled or replaced.

Android phone and TV. VortX-0.4.0-full-mpv-universal.apk includes VortX Player/MPV. VortX-0.4.0-play-media3-universal.apk is the Media3 variant. Both APKs include the supported architectures; choose the variant you already use to retain its normal update path. The Play bundle is also attached for its distribution workflow.

Check SHA256SUMS-ci.txt for Apple downloads and SHA256SUMS-android.txt with SIGNING_PROVENANCE.txt for Android.

0.4.0 Beta 12 - Apple playback recovery, add-on sync, and Usenet:

Install this over any earlier build. Beta 12 brings together the Apple fixes and features landed since Beta 10: playback-state recovery, more reliable add-on ordering and watch-state sync, artwork repairs, multiple Usenet servers, direct NZB indexers, and related titles. Apple build 245.

Beta 11 did not publish: its packaging run ran out of disk space. This release uses a fresh tag and fresh packages from current source, including the later fixes. It is promoted as Latest while retaining its beta name. Apple TV, iPhone, iPad, and Mac are included; Android is not attached.

What's new:

Keep more than one Usenet server. Save, edit, disable, remove, and prioritize multiple NNTP servers. Existing single-server settings migrate. The resolver preserves the servers supplied by your add-on, then tries your ordered saved servers, then the existing TorBox cloud fallback when configured. Credentials stay in account-scoped secure storage. TorBox cloud fallback requires its API key and may need to prepare an uncached job; it is not a promise of instant playback from every provider.

Search NZBGeek and other Newznab indexers directly. Indexer settings now feed the normal Apple source lists. A series search uses the episode you selected, not a stale watched episode, and completed empty searches do not keep restarting. Requests and results are scoped to the active account, profile, and configuration. HTTPS credentials and NZB links are excluded from diagnostics and settings backups.

Open prequels, sequels, and collection neighbors. Apple detail pages now expose explicit related-title links supplied by add-ons. Known TMDB movie collections also show adjacent releases by date. This is not a complete anime relationship database or an inferred story chronology.

What's fixed:

An interrupted AVPlayer seek can recover instead of silently hanging. A current seek could return “not completed” after its recovery deadline had already been cancelled, leaving neither a successful landing nor a recovery owner. The completion now checks the exact request, item, and load first. An interrupted current seek uses the existing target-owned remux recovery; a direct asset reports a retryable seek error. Old callbacks cannot cancel a newer seek, restore an obsolete position, or manufacture an episode ending. Committed pause state and track choices are retained.

Paused seeks show the position and subtitle cue where the player actually landed. AVPlayer can land slightly away from the requested time. The producer's buffer accounting already used that actual landing, but the paused controls and cue could keep showing the requested position until another clock tick. They now use the same accepted landing.

A rejected retry no longer leaves the old video under a new spinner. Apple TV used to clear the live surface and start a fresh load timeout even if the engine refused the replacement. State resets, selection restoration, and the new timeout now belong only to an accepted load. A refused load also retains the current resume-seek watchdog instead of cancelling the last recovery owner.

Pause, Play, and old end-of-episode work stay with their own playback session. Play during a paused remux recovery publishes the resumed intent before waiting for restoration. Rewinding cancels the previous paused EOF and its tail recovery; an old same-item callback cannot restart from the wrong point or jump to the next episode. Blocked seek admission has a request-owned deadline, and successful seeks immediately reconcile the producer's retained buffer even while paused. These are targeted state and liveness fixes, not a longer generic stall timer.

Changing players uses the current source. AVPlayer and VortX Player handoffs retain the selected URL, request headers, episode, position, and transport intent. A late frame from the old mount cannot cancel a fresh-link recovery. Selecting an already-mounted engine with a newly resolved URL issues that load instead of silently ignoring it. This includes the provider-reconnect path used by TorBox.

Startup keeps a valid video surface intact. The drawable is sized before mpv initialization. The first layout no longer tears down an already-valid decoder with a video-track reset; a genuinely unsized surface still has its one-shot recovery. Mac backing-scale changes use the native resize/wake path. This removes a concrete source of avoidable startup work without pretending every reported ten-second start has the same cause.

Hardware decoding has a second hardware route before software. Apple devices try direct VideoToolbox, then VideoToolbox copy-back when direct surface import is unavailable. Explicit decoder overrides remain respected. Simulators retain their separate direct-only policy because their upload limitation is different. Diagnostics refresh codec and pixel-format evidence after reconfiguration so later fallback reports describe the active state.

Native subtitle backgrounds respect the selected style more closely. Both text-background attributes are now set explicitly: the enclosing subtitle window is transparent, while the selected outline, shaded, or box style controls the character background. This preserves the earlier single-renderer fix. Authored or bitmap subtitles and system accessibility overrides can still affect the result.

NNTP reads are allowed to keep making progress. A continuously downloading article could be cancelled by an absolute 20-second timer. Nonempty incoming data now renews the inactivity timer, with a separate overall safety bound and article-size ceiling still enforced. Completion, cancellation, and failure retire both timers. Healthy foreground pauses retain useful NNTP data. Existing archive, byte-range, seek, reopen, and provider-failover protections remain in place; live throughput and article availability still matter.

Continue Watching can repair its episode list without losing the selected episode. Refresh accepts a valid initially unloaded model and binds returned metadata to the exact series and episode request. Stale refresh callbacks cannot overwrite a newer request. Temporarily missing metadata no longer discards a matching watched-completion intent; a later explicit unwatch cancels that intent rather than having it replay unexpectedly.

Your add-on order is an explicit choice, not response timing. A routine sync cannot replace a newer peer order with this device's stale applied order, and a partial engine snapshot cannot shrink the saved roster. Failed uploads retain pending reorder intent; delayed acknowledgements cannot erase a newer edit. Source groups follow the app's add-on order, and reordering invalidates the live source cache so slow responses do not determine placement.

Turning off Stremio mirroring actually keeps VortX-owned changes local. Installing, restoring, removing, and replacing app-owned add-ons use local collection actions when mirroring is disabled. Routine refresh respects the setting, while deliberate Stremio import remains available. Changing an add-on URL validates the replacement before removing the working descriptor and preserves its slot.

QR add-on pairing keeps the authority issued by the relay. Claim and acknowledgement use the correct paired-session authority instead of losing it between steps.

Library progress and watched actions merge as complete observations. Episode, position, duration, and timestamp travel together. Newer peer progress can update Continue Watching cards and resume selection without overriding active playback or explicit local rewinds. Owner and profile watched/unwatched actions carry causal receipts, badges read the merged state, and whole-season marking writes the history carrier once. Durable watched history is kept separately from the short Continue Watching rail.

Late artwork reaches the screen, including episode images and heroes. Same-title updates now publish changed posters, backgrounds, logos, episode inventories, thumbnails, and trailers after the original model has appeared. Large-image decode permits remain held for the full load. This fixes publication and resource-accounting defects, not absent upstream images.

Trakt Continue Watching can resolve its supplied artwork. Scheme-less image URLs are accepted, local library art is available as a fallback, and cached aliases join only the exact title instead of unrelated same-name entries.

Apple TV contribution receipts stop growing an oversized preferences value. Successful source receipts move into an atomic file, with verified migration and a small recovery marker, instead of accumulating tens of thousands of entries in UserDefaults.

Seek-preview failures no longer trigger a retry storm. Generation-aware cancellation and bounded backoff preserve later recovery without repeatedly hammering an unavailable preview source. A missing community preview is still reported honestly rather than invented.

Website and account:

The separately deployed vortx.tv dashboard update is retained: one-time Stremio import uses the official API directly, preserves the entered password exactly without storing it, and distinguishes credentials, network, and malformed-response failures. Cancellation or account changes invalidate older attempts. Dashboard add-on edits are serialized, preserve ownership and order, and refresh from the encrypted account document.

An account save is not proof that every device installed a manifest. The separately hosted manifest proxy and any remaining cross-device conflict still need their own evidence; this release does not claim to have repaired an unidentified proxy deployment.

Verification and limits:

Public packaging is bound to the immutable tag, build number, package metadata, checksums, and signed feed receipt. The workflow verifies the install-feed routes before publishing and checks the public assets afterward. It reclaims finished build inputs before creating the Mac disk image and verifies the Mac ad-hoc signature.

Physical Apple TV testing remains essential for sustained Dolby Vision playback, real-provider NNTP throughput, frame pacing, pause/seek/source switching, and the exact ten-second-start report. The separate iOS pre-player crash report has no captured stack establishing its cause and is not labelled fixed by this beta. Passing synthetic fixtures is not a guarantee that every field playback failure is resolved.

Android:

No Android package is attached to this Apple-priority beta. The source retains the bounded split-audio trailer-loading correction, but broader Android MPV/audio stability, remote focus, Back handling, Shield testing, and Apple-style detail/hero and feature parity remain follow-up work. No unverified percentage-complete claim is made.

Please test:

• Resume a series from Continue Watching, seek backward while paused, press Play, then use Next and Previous. Confirm the right episode, position, and watched mark.
• Pause a compatible Dolby Vision title, resume it, and switch players or sources. Export this build's diagnostic if it freezes, reconnects, or falls back.
• Test fresh starts and high-bitrate playback, including a source that uses VideoToolbox copy-back.
• Reorder, remove, reinstall, and replace add-ons on two updated devices, including offline changes and relaunch. Check source-group order as well as the add-on list.
• Test watched/unwatched changes and library/CW progress across TV, phone, and Mac.
• Try your prioritized NNTP servers and NZBGeek/Newznab searches, including an episode advance, pause, and backward seek.
• Check the previously missing anime artwork, Trakt thumbnails, related-title links, QR pairing, and native subtitle background style.

apps.name: JESSI
apps.subtitle: JESSI (Java Edition Servers Suck on Ios) is a jailed app for ios 14+ that runs minecraft servers directly on device!
apps.localizedDescription:
Basic Information:

JESSI is an iOS app that runs Minecraft: Java Edition servers natively on iOS, targeting iOS 14+. JESSI runs on both jailed and jailbroken iOS, only requiring JIT to do so.

JESSI was designed specifically to be as easy to use as possible, even if you have never hosted a Minecraft server before. The UI is simple to understand and use, making JESSI the best beginner friendly option to host a minecraft server.

JESSI is still being actively developed, and plenty of more features will come. Here's a list of some of JESSI's most important features:

• Ability to run minecraft servers (duh).

• Server memory allocation slider.
• Easy to use server creator, with support for several server softwares.
• A file manager that allows you to easily manage several servers.

versions.localizedDescription:
Changelog:

Java 25 support (required for minecraft 26.1+).

there haven't been many changes since the release candidate, it's only really been a few minor bug fixes. Since this is the 1.0 release, here's the list of most important features in the app:

• Ability to run minecraft servers (duh).

• Server memory allocation slider.
• Easy to use server creator, with support for several server softwares.
• A file manager that allows you to easily manage several servers.
• Network tunneling via playit.gg and UPnP support.

• Keep alive, run the server in the background even with the screen off.
• Server config GUI.

thank you to all of the beta testers!

Changelog:

• Proper TrollStore support, TrollStore devices will now spawn the JVM in a seperate process, meaning you can freely stop/start the server without the app closing.
• Keep Alive, JESSI can now run in the background, even in LiveContainer or if the screen is off!
• UI improvements and bugfixes.
• There is now a built in tutorial in the app! On first app launch, you will be given a welcome message and be prompted to take a tour around the app.

• Some easter eggs have been added:eyes:.
• Removed Herobrine.

apps.localizedDescription:
Website:

https://mirarr-app.github.io/mirarr/

Available on Android, Windows, Linux , IOS and Web.:

This is a movie app that aims to simplify the process of watching movies and TV shows.

Features:

• Trending movies and TV shows.
• Seperate movies and TV shows by genre.
• Watchlist, Favorites and Rating.

• External links to movies and TV shows to watch.
• External links to get the movies and TV shows.

Some stuff needs extra love:

The app supports custom styles for special movies and TV shows that have enough character.

versions.localizedDescription:
• Fix text in profile page and discover page being not readable.
• Fix omarchy theme path to align with Omarchy Quattro.

Performance Improvements:

• Offloaded watch history SQLite operations to a dedicated isolate to prevent UI thread blocking.
• Deferred non-essential startup tasks until after the first frame paint.
• Routed HTTP calls through a shared ApiClient singleton with connection reuse and timeouts.
• Reduced detail page network requests by combining TMDB endpoints via append_to_response.
• Scoped state rebuilds on detail pages, search tab switching, main shell, and theme settings.
• Replaced live BackdropFilter blurs on bars, badges, and backgrounds with solid overlays.
• Batched watch history updates for series and seasons into single database transactions.
• Optimized shelf rendering using static skeletons, memCacheWidth poster sizing, and fixed item extents.
• Added in-memory caching for web Hive watch history and region-sensitive Futures.
• Streamlined watchlist loading by fetching pagination pages concurrently.

Bug Fixes & Refactoring:

• Fixed missing dart:ui imports required for PointerDeviceKind scroll behavior.
• Hardened search against stale API responses and query encoding errors.
• Fixed mobile movie detail layout constraints and removed intrusive network error dialogs.
• Resolved assertion errors in series season dropdowns within the F2M section.

• Skeletonized genre headers on home shelves while names are loading.
• Aligned series detail app bar colors, shelf contrast, and desktop action buttons with movie pages.

Asset Cleanup:

• Removed custom fonts and google_fonts dependency.

Features:

• Added Material You dynamic color themeing support on Android devices in Settings under Theme section. It extracts system wallpaper colors to dynamically tint application accents.

UI Improvements:

• Redesigned quick action buttons (Favorite, Watchlist, Share, Rate, and Mark as Watched) on Movie and Series detail pages using Material 3 Expressive floating glass containers and pill badges.
• Replaced standard loading spinners with custom Material 3 Expressive loading indicators across detail pages, bottom navigation, cast and crew details, and gallery pages.
• Redesigned confirmation popups and alert dialogs (Logout, Delete Watch Log, Network Errors, Fetch Watch Times, and Update) with Material 3 Expressive shapes, header icons, and pill action buttons.
• Standardized card grid spacing in profile page to match main and series pages.
• Adjusted trending movies row alignment to match standard layout margins.
• Improved upcoming episode countdown text layout and typography in the watchlist calendar.
• Improved button text layout and padding in settings screen.
• Added Iran region movie watch page with F2M integration, direct server options, and streaming links. Access by tapping Watch when region is set to Iran.

• Fixed desktop action pill buttons stretching to full screen width.
• Improved F2M link parser to format quality as main title, convert dub/sub attributes into English tag chips, and translate Persian season numbers.

Misc:

• Replaced SingleChildScrollView layouts with lazy CustomScrollView and SliverList builders in main movies and series pages.
• Replaced BackdropFilter GPU blur overlays with semi-transparent container styling across movie and series cards.
• Added memCacheWidth constraints and downscaled poster and backdrop image resolutions to reduce RAM and VRAM consumption.
• Offloaded cast and crew loading in detail pages to non-blocking asynchronous streams with shimmer skeleton placeholders and virtualized ListView builders.
• Extracted movie action buttons into isolated stateful widgets to prevent full-page rebuilds on user interactions.
• Removed N+1 HTTP request waterfalls in series watch toggle by computing total episode counts from series details.
• Batched SQLite watch history checks in season and episode detail sheets.
• Added RepaintBoundary wrappers around backdrop headers to isolate GPU paint layers.
• Removed Isolate.spawn overhead for lightweight TMDB API JSON parsing.
• Added M3 expressive components including rating bar, interactive container, and page transition utilities.
• Redesigned share menu on mobile detail pages to pop out directly from the share button.
• Added Mirarr WebApp link sharing option alongside Cover Art and TMDB link options.
• Added deep link support for Mirarr WebApp URLs on Android and Web so shared links open directly to the specified movie or TV show.

apps.name: Kodi
apps.subtitle: Media center for all your digital entertainment
apps.localizedDescription:
Kodi can be used to play almost all popular audio and video formats around. It was designed for network playback, so you can stream your multimedia from anywhere in the house or directly from the internet using practically any protocol available.

THis build is distributed by a third-party not related to Kodi/XMBC.

Point Kodi to your media and watch it scan and automagically create a personalized library complete with box covers, descriptions, and fanart. There are playlist and slideshow functions, a weather forecast feature and many audio visualizations. Once installed, your computer or HTPC will become a fully functional multimedia jukebox.

versions.localizedDescription:
Major user-facing changes include:

Video.

• Added HDR support on Xbox One.
• Fixed Blu-ray playback on Linux.
• Fixed handling of HDR10 light metadata changes.
• Fixed subtitle selection for ISO 639-1 (two-letter) language codes.

Library/Sources and Management.

• Improved speed of video library rescans.
• Fixed multi-episode files overwriting the first episode.
• Fixed info dialog for certain Movie Versions.
• Fixed some false positives detecting Movie Versions.

Music.

• Fixed CDDB lookups using Gnudb.org's CDDB API.
• Fixed album search failing for artist names.

Audio.

• Fixed rare Pipewire crash when connecting/removing audio devices.

PVR.

• Fixed crash when a PVR stream is stopped via remote app.

Peripherals.

• Added support for Turkish keyboards on Linux.
• Fixed enabling and disabling Pulse-Eight CEC adapters.
• Fixed the Delete and Alternative Insert keys on macOS.
• Fixed minor visual glitches when managing peripherals.

Addons.

• Fixed updating add-ons after 25 days of inactivity (extended to ~68 years).

Skin/GUI.

• Fixed busy dialog crash when multiple dialogs are opened.
• Fixed suspend dialog remaining open after the system wakes up.
• Improved touch support for slider dialog arrows.

Network.

• Added support for HTTP Basic Authentication.
• Fixed some network streams failing due to interrupted HTTP/2 transfers.
• Updated libnfs to v6 for embedded platforms.
• Updated CA certificates to 2025-07-15 from the Mozilla CA certificate store.

apps.name: Synkplay
apps.subtitle: 📱 Syncplay Mobile (now Synkplay) is a Syncplay client app for Android and iOS. Watch stuff in sync with your friends. Compatible with the official Syncplay for PC. Fully written in Kotlin and Compose multiplatform
apps.localizedDescription: 📱 Syncplay Mobile (now Synkplay) is a Syncplay client app for Android and iOS. Watch stuff in sync with your friends. Compatible with the official Syncplay for PC. Fully written in Kotlin and Compose multiplatform.

versions.localizedDescription:
The new look:

• The whole app was redrawn: one set of controls, five text sizes, colours that come from the theme, and frosted panels over the video on devices that can draw them.
• Home is a single form: your name, the server, the player, and Join. It fits a phone, a phone on its side, a tablet or a desktop window.
• The room has a rail for its actions and a status line. The controls hide while the video plays and come back on a tap.
• Settings have a search box, grouped rows, values in units people actually read, and colours you edit in place. Each player's settings sit inside the player category.
• Themes preview as a miniature of the app, and the theme creator shows what a seed colour will do before you save.
• Motion can be reduced from settings. A screen reader announces who is ready, connection changes and new messages.
• Watching alone has its own row in About: tap the logo on Home.

Players:

• KitePlayer, a new engine written for this app on top of FFmpeg, is available on Android, iOS and desktop as an experimental choice. It has chapters, external and styled subtitles, pitch-preserved speed from 0.25x to 4x, and plays links over https.
• Three engines per platform: ExoPlayer, mpv and KitePlayer on Android, and the system player, VLCKit and KitePlayer on iOS. VLC on Android and mpv on iOS are gone. VLCKit is the iOS default.
• Volume can go past 100 on players that can boost (mpv, ExoPlayer, VLCKit). The device volume fills first, then the player's own gain takes over.
• Double taps add up to one jump, and a long press shows where a seek will land before it commits.
• When you watch alone, the app remembers where you left a file and offers to continue from there.
• Seeking with KitePlayer lands on the exact frame in one step and is about twice as fast. Files with tens of thousands of subtitle lines no longer slow it down.
• YouTube links work again with the updated extractor, and a friend's YouTube link in the shared playlist is accepted without any setup. SoundCloud, PeerTube, Bandcamp and media.ccc.de links work the same way on Android and desktop. iOS handles YouTube only.

Sync and playback:

• Fixed the phantom pause: a player stopping on its own no longer pauses the whole room.
• The room shows when it is waiting for the video instead of looking frozen, and says who it is waiting for before playback starts.
• Audio and subtitle picks survive a reload on every engine, and follow your preferred languages.
• Tracks marked as accessibility captions, audio description or forced now say so in the picker.
• When a file ends, the playlist moves on once, not once per person in the room.
• A file that is still opening no longer drags the whole room back to the start.
• If you load your file after the room has already started, you now sync to the room instead of sitting paused at the start.
• A per-user time offset lets two different rips of the same film be watched together.
• The three drift thresholds (rewind, slowdown, fast-forward) are now settings.
• A phone coming back from the background follows the room instead of dragging it back.

Room and chat:

• Volume and brightness have their own controls, so a swipe is no longer the only way.
• You can mute someone, and image links from other people stay hidden until you tap them.
• The user list has a compact view and a detailed one. The detailed view shows each person's file, its length, its size and whether it matches yours.
• A playlist change can be undone.
• Picture in picture grows out of the video instead of popping up from nowhere.
• The room can follow the device's rotation or stay in landscape. There is a setting for it.
• Android: lock screen and headset controls work in the room and follow the same readiness rules as the play button.
• On a television, the room's controls stay inside the visible area.
• The locked screen tells you how to unlock it.
• The room shows whether your connection is encrypted.
• Panels look right on a light theme.
• Buffering no longer pushes the play button around. The button rounds into a circle and its colours move until the player catches up.
• The custom skip button sits between the two jump buttons.

• A bug report sent from the app says which engine, which build and which device.

Connection:

• Encrypted connections now check the server's certificate against the name you typed.
• You can require encryption. A server that offers none is refused before anything is sent.
• A dropped connection reconnects with a growing wait instead of hammering the server.
• A handshake that never finishes gives up instead of hanging.
• Leaving the server address empty joins the official server, as it always looked like it would.
• The network you are on can no longer push the app's own services onto plain HTTP.
• A pasted link is checked against the site it really points to, not the text shown in front of it.

Hosting:

• Hosting lives on the home screen now, under the server choice, with the address first.
• The hosting screen and its notification use the app's language.
• A silent client is dropped after the timeout the server already advertised.
• An operator password works only for the room it belongs to.
• Creating a managed room now really puts the password on your clipboard, which it has claimed to do for a long time.

Language:

• Change the app's language from settings, on every platform, with no restart.
• All seven translations are complete: Arabic, German, Spanish, French, Polish, Russian and Chinese.
• Audio and subtitle language names are shown in your own language.
• A crash when opening settings, caused by a string defined twice, is fixed. Strings are now generated at build time and checked for duplicates.

Elsewhere:

• Invite links: share a room with a link, and open one to join.

• Settings can be exported to a file and imported back.
• A damaged settings file no longer crashes the app at launch. It starts on defaults and tells you.
• Service keys are never written to the log, so a log you share carries none.
• You can tell the GIF service to forget you between sessions.
• Reading settings at startup no longer blocks drawing, and neither does logging.
• Android 13 and up can theme the launcher icon.

Protocol and stability release. Fixes false file mismatch warnings, disconnect loops, crashes, and memory leaks.

Synkplay is on the Apple App Store and Google Play.

File matching:

• Fixed file privacy modes breaking sync checks with PC users. Hashed file names now follow the same logic as the PC client.
• Fixed false "file mismatch" warnings. Comparison now ignores letter case, checks raw names against hashed ones, and allows a difference in length of up to 2.5 seconds.

Connection and protocol:

• Fixed server messages being handled out of order. They are now strictly in order, matching the PC client, which removes subtle sync glitches under load.

• Fixed a disconnect loop in large rooms, caused by an inbound message buffer that was too small.
• Fixed a crash when the encrypted connection fails to negotiate. A bad server certificate now shows a connection failure and retries.

• Fixed messages that carry several commands at once. All of them are handled now, not just the first.

• Fixed server error messages such as "Wrong password supplied" failing silently into an endless reconnect loop. They now appear in the room.
• Removed a pointless 100 ms delay per message on the Ktor network engine. It slowed room joins and skewed latency readings.

Rooms and playlists:

• Fixed users who switch rooms lingering in the user list for up to 15 seconds. They now appear and disappear right away.

• Added shared playlist limits of 250 items and 10,000 characters, with a warning up front, matching the official server. The built-in server applies the same limits to incoming playlists.
• Added the ability for controllers to set other users' readiness across clients. The setOthersReadiness capability is advertised both ways, and the room sees "X was set as ready by Y".
• Fixed trusted domains being too loose. They now match the PC client exactly: exact host, the www version, *. wildcards, and path prefixes. Random subdomains are no longer trusted.

Crashes and leaks:

• Android: fixed a native thread leak on every reconnect attempt.
• iOS: fixed memory leaks when leaving a room. All three player engines now shut their position trackers down properly.
• Fixed a possible crash when leaving a room while the player engine fails to shut down.
• iOS: fixed mpv playing by itself right after loading media. It now waits for the room or for you to unpause, matching Android.

Translations:

Help translate at Weblate. You can translate existing text or add a whole new language. Strings change often, so some languages fall behind.

Android: how to install:

The app is on Google Play, but releases there can be held up by review times. Downloading the APK here always gets you the newest version.

Not sure which APK? Use universal. Most modern phones should use arm64-v8a. If that does not work, try armeabi-v7a. There are x86_64 and x86 builds too.

Want a smaller app? syncplay-version-exo-only.apk is the smallest option. Otherwise the full APK adds mpv and VLC, which are the stronger video engines.

Adds mpv on iOS as the new default engine. Fixes millisecond-accurate sync on Android mpv, plus bugs in every other engine.

Synkplay is on the Apple App Store and Google Play.

New iOS engine: mpv:

mpv is now on iOS through MPVKit. It is experimental, and it is the new default.

In testing it is noticeably faster and more forgiving than VLC, which caused sync bugs because it does not report its playback position reliably. mpv on iOS should be about as stable as it is on Android, but with fewer features. There is no Lua support, for example.

The same in-room mpv settings from Android appear here, with no promise yet that each one works. Subtitles work, both built-in and external files. Network media is not tested. Use VLC if you need to play a URL.

mpv on Android:

• Fixed playback position being rounded to whole seconds. It is now millisecond-precise. The old rounding made everyone in the room speed up or slow down slightly almost every second.
• Fixed wrong or empty audio and subtitle track names when the language or the title was missing.

ExoPlayer on Android:

• Fixed audio track selection writing to the wrong field, which also wiped your saved subtitle choice.
• Fixed an invalid buffer setting combination crashing playback. Values are now clamped.

AVPlayer on iOS:

• Fixed buffering being counted as playing.
• Fixed a backwards check that left the audio and subtitle lists empty.

VLCKit on iOS:

• Fixed a zero or stale position being reported during buffering.
• Fixed brief false pause events. They are now debounced.
• Fixed a stray stop event being treated as the end of the file.
• Fixed a seek permanently breaking position reporting.

All engines:

• Made the audio and subtitle track lists scrollable.
• Improved handling of external subtitle file extensions.

Sync changes:

• Fixed a phantom duplicate seek, and removed the redundant sync code behind it.
• Fixed file names not matching between mobile Synkplay users and PC Syncplay users when names are hashed.

• Trusted only http and https domains by default now.
• Fixed auto-reconnect giving up after a single failed try. The retry interval is also clamped, so it cannot loop at zero delay.
• Limited fast-forward-on-desync to followers in controlled rooms, matching the PC client. It used to yank normal-room clients forward on any sustained lag.
• Fixed the app losing its encrypted connection after reconnecting.
• Fixed IfMinUsersReady ignoring the "already ready" gate.
• Stopped backgrounded clients from broadcasting playback control.
• Made pause-on-leave apply only on your own device.

Translations:

Help translate at Weblate. You can translate existing text or add a whole new language. Strings change often, so some languages fall behind.

Android: how to install:

The app is on Google Play, but that build can be out of date, since Google takes a while to review. Downloading the APK here is always best.

Not sure about your phone? The universal APK works everywhere, but it is the biggest download. Most modern phones can use arm64-v8a instead, which is much smaller. If that fails, try armeabi-v7a. Rare devices like x86_64 and x86 have their own builds.

Want a smaller app? syncplay-version-exo-only.apk has ExoPlayer alone. It is the lightest build and works nearly everywhere. The full APK is still worth it for mpv, which plays almost any format.

apps.name: NOOP
apps.subtitle: Offline WHOOP companion — pair your strap over Bluetooth, keep all data on your own device. No cloud, no account, no subscription
apps.localizedDescription:
Raw data capture ·.

First launch on macOS. NOOP is not notarized by Apple — notarization needs a paid Apple Developer ID tied to a real identity, which doesn't fit an anonymous, free project. The app is sandboxed and ad-hoc code-signed, and the full source is here to inspect. Because it isn't notarized, macOS Gatekeeper blocks it on first open (you may see "damaged" or "unverified developer" — that's the download quarantine flag, not real damage). To open it, do one of these once:

• Terminal (most reliable): drag NOOP.app to Applications, then run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/NOOP.app and open NOOP normally.

versions.localizedDescription:
Rolling latest testing build — refreshed in place, so this tag is always the newest. NOOP main + ryanbr's open PRs + vetted community PRs, built with the NOOP Staging identity (installs beside the official app, separate data). Filenames carry the base app version (v11.7.0).

• Android (debug) — NOOP-android-debug-v11.7.0.apk — debuggable build. com.noop.whoop.debug.
• macOS — NOOP-macos-v11.7.0.zip — unzip, then right-click → Open (ad-hoc signed, not notarized; Gatekeeper warns once). If it says "damaged", run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/NOOP.app.
• iOS — NOOP-ios-unsigned-v11.7.0.ipa — sideload via AltStore / Sideloadly (re-signs on-device); embedded watch app stripped, widget extension retained for Home/Lock-Screen widgets and Live Activities.

Base app version 11.7.0 · built 2026-09-15 · c430ca0.

NOOP v11.7.0:

A release about the app keeping up with you, and about readings meaning what they say.

A stress screen that keeps up:

Scoring a day of stress reads hundreds of thousands of samples. That work was happening on the same thread that draws the screen, so Today and Stress could sit unresponsive while they loaded. It now runs off that thread on both platforms, the baseline is reduced a day at a time rather than held a month at once, and the unprompted rescore yields to whatever you are doing instead of competing with it for the machine.

The home-screen widget fills on its own schedule without the app being opened. A rescore that produces nothing is retried rather than being allowed to spend the whole refresh interval, and the Today curve is kept as fresh as the screen it links to.

The readings themselves now agree with each other. The 0 to 3 level has one spelling across the widget and the card, and is no longer rounded a second time on its way to the widget. The screen draws its line from the same sliding read the number is taken from. Movement is drawn as the stretches it actually covers rather than as dots on the axis. An early morning says the day has not started rather than reporting Calibrating, which reads like something is wrong.

WHOOP 5 readings in the units the strap sends:

Thanks to @Trillient, two decoding faults are corrected.

R-R intervals arriving on the standard heart-rate profile were converted as though they were in the Bluetooth spec's units. A WHOOP 5 sends milliseconds directly, so every interval taken from that profile came out 2.3% low, and HRV computed from it inherited the error. What settled it was a paired capture: the same beats arriving on both the strap's own channel and the standard one carry byte-identical values, so only one of the two conversions could be right.

The console log's record header was read as a 16-bit counter spanning two bytes. Only the first is a counter, and it wraps at 255. Across 2,978 records from a single night the second byte never moved through nine of those wraps, which a real counter could not do. Both platforms now decode the two fields separately.

An Oura ring that stops repeating itself:

Thanks to @pipiche38 for a sustained run of corrections to the ring's history path.

A replayed burst that the ring's own clock disproves as a reboot no longer resets the history resume cursor, and no longer announces a reboot that did not happen. A night that has just been offloaded is scored immediately rather than waiting for the next periodic tick. History is fetched every five minutes rather than every fifteen, the anchor check judges a ten second gap rather than only a thirty second one, and an onset rekey is refused when the assembler's own clip never bound.

There is also a feature-mode control and a consolidated set of Oura diagnostics in the Test Centre, the raw night sidecar stays in the export, and the SpO2 sample keeps only the channel that carries a reading.

Scores that survive a re-score:

Thanks to @bhelm. WHOOP 5 HRV and Recovery, and the vitals derived from R-R, were being dropped by a re-score pass that could not recompute them, so a value you already had could disappear on a pass that had nothing better to put in its place. Both are now preserved.

Readings that say when they are at a limit:

A Fitness Age resting at the end of its scale now says so, rather than presenting a bound as though it were a measurement, and points at the number that still moves when the age stops. On Sleep, a night already detected and staged no longer sits under a banner claiming it is still being calculated, and browsing back to a night with no stage data no longer shows the most recent night's date beneath it.

Diagnostics that name the cause:

A device reporting no R-R now says whether the beats were never banked or were refused by the unit policy, which are different problems with different answers. The nightly HRV summary says why it reported nothing. A retired probe tells whoever reads its output which switch to turn on, and stops under-reporting its own retirement. A re-arm clears a refusal latch that previously could not be reached once set. The sync chip surfaces the strap's backlog.

Thanks:

Thanks to @pipiche38 (Oura history, replay judgement, diagnostics and export), @Trillient (WHOOP 5 R-R units and console sequence decoding), @bhelm (preserving legacy HRV, Recovery and R-R vitals), @kavemang (tile values that shrink rather than truncate, per-signal illness baselines, Android guards), and @digitalerdude (parity tooling on macOS, sync chip backlog, and documentation that describes what the code returns).

• fix(android): skip stress scoring without a widget.
• fix(android): guard sleep session cache upserts.
• feat(oura): add a SetFeatureMode enable control, consolidate Oura Test Centre diagnostics.
• today(android): move Customize into the header cluster, where it stops covering the wordmark.
• today(android): shape a hosted card clip from what it actually renders.
• stress: reduce each baseline day as it is read, instead of holding thirty at once.
• diag: say whether a device R-R beats were never banked or were refused by the unit policy.
• Preserve legacy WHOOP 5 HRV and Recovery across re-score.
• widget: retry a stress rescore that produced nothing, instead of spending the interval on it.
• fix(oura): don't reset the history resume cursor to 0 on a stale replay the ring's own clock disproves as a reboot.
• sleep: a night already in hand silences the calculating banner.
• stress: draw the movement marks as the stretches they are, not as dots on the axis.
• hrv: say why the nightly summary reported nothing.
• illness: a handful of stored nights is not a baseline.
• Describe what DayOwnerSource.candidatePriorities actually returns (#2026).
• probe: let a re-arm clear the refusal latch it could never reach.
• Preserve legacy RR-derived vitals and remove accidental scaffolding.
• ci: let the parity gate see main, so drift stops ambushing other PRs.
• Sync chip: surface the strap backlog, with both counts inflected (#833).
• Say that the day-owner path uses archived candidates, not just inherits them (#2026).
• ble: tell a retired probe reader to turn the switch ON, and stop under-reporting retirement.
• parity tests: pass on macOS, and resolve expand_twin_map's root (#2143 follow-up).
• parity_ledger: resolve the temp checkout root before deriving from it (#2143).
• fix(diagnostics): keep the night's raw Oura sidecar in the export — session-scoped, ring-buffered, fairly capped, generations merged.

• fix(oura): score the ring's freshly-offloaded night now, not at the next periodic tick.
• fix(oura): refuse the #1284 onset rekey when the assembler's own clip never bound.
• fix(oura): only persist the SpO2 raw channel, drop dc_raw from spo2Sample.
• fix(oura): fetch ring history every 5 min, not 15 — the periodic fetch is the real data cadence.
• fix(oura): let the #2097 anchor check judge a 10 s gap, not only 30 s.
• health: trust Android baselines per signal.
• stress: one spelling for the 0-3 level, on the widget and the card.
• stress: stop the widget snapshot rounding the level a second time.
• stress: give the marker tile's reading the width the chip was holding.

• health: say when a Fitness Age is sitting on the end of its scale.
• stress: keep the Today curve as fresh as the screen it links to.
• today: put scan and connect on the Today header.
• today: show the scan control only while the strap is away, and make it look like a scan.
• stress: do not say Calibrating when the day has simply not started yet.
• widget: refresh the stress curve without waiting for the app to be opened.
• fix(oura): stop announcing a ring reboot the #2097 judge has just rejected.
• health: point at the number that still moves when the age stops.
• stress: draw the screen's line from the sliding read, not the bare hours.
• stress: get the screen's work off the main thread and the chart out from behind it.
• today: stop scoring a day of heart rate on the UI thread.
• fix: decode WHOOP 5 console sequence as a wrapping u8.
• fix: WHOOP 5 R-R words are milliseconds, not 1/1024-second ticks.
• whoop5: decode the Kotlin console sequence as a wrapping u8.
• whoop5: pin the Kotlin console sequence wrap, matching Swift.
• test(ios): make the reject-archive protection skip visible on macOS.
• test(import): assert the Inbox purge no-op off iOS instead of skipping it.
• sleep: date the browsed night, not the newest one, in the nav header.
• perf: let the unprompted analysis work actually yield to the UI.
• ui: shrink ellipsized stat values.
• ui: test the stat-value shrink rule, and guard the line index.

Downloads — NOOP Staging identity, installs beside the official app (separate data):

• Android — NOOP-android-v11.7.0.apk (com.noop.whoop.staging).
• macOS — NOOP-macos-v11.7.0.zip (unzip, then right-click → Open).
• iOS — NOOP-ios-unsigned-v11.7.0.ipa (AltStore / Sideloadly).

NOOP v11.6.0:

A release about putting the day's readings where you actually look, and about being honest when a reading is missing rather than drawing over the hole.

A Today screen you arrange yourself:

Today's stress curve and the Trends charts are no longer locked to their own tabs. Both can be hosted on Today as cards, on Apple and on Android, so the screen you open first carries the things you check first. A hosted card opens the tab it came from when you tap it, so it is a shortcut rather than a dead end, and on the classic Today a hero ring now opens its own detail.

There is also a stress widget on both platforms, showing today's hourly curve on the home screen. It fills on its own schedule without the app being opened, and when there is nothing to show it explains why instead of leaving you looking at an empty box.

Charts that break where the strap did:

A heart-rate line used to draw straight across hours the strap never recorded, which quietly asserted a reading that was never taken. Those runs are now broken wherever the gap is real, on every surface that draws a heart-rate trace rather than only the one where it was first noticed.

WHOOP 5 readings corrected:

Thanks to @Trillient, R-R intervals from a WHOOP 5 are now read in the units the strap actually sends, which is the input HRV is computed from. Skin temperature now reaches recovery scoring before the score is computed rather than arriving after it. Both platforms carry regression tests covering the gaps these were found in.

Backups that check themselves:

An export now verifies the file it actually wrote, on every path that writes one, so a backup that was truncated is caught at the moment it is made instead of the moment you need it. When the database itself reports a problem, the full text of what SQLite said is shown in something that can hold it and copied, rather than clipped to a line that leaves out the part that mattered.

A coach that holds on to your conversation:

A rejected API key can be corrected in place without losing the conversation you were in. The coach is told what the workout was rather than only that one happened, the consent screen describes what it actually sends, and the morning brief now reaches the screen it was generated for.

Diagnostics that say why:

A night that missed the re-score cache now names the setting that dropped it, instead of reporting only how many nights missed. A dropped link is always recorded, the Live Console reads the device you selected rather than whichever field happened to be populated, and the Rest card says why it is waiting on a sync instead of changing in silence.

Oura logs keep your serial out of them: serials are masked in the redactors on both platforms, and product-info replies no longer reach the raw diagnostics sidecar. Both from @pipiche38.

The Test Centre now hands you its bundle through the same share sheet the strap log uses and stops there, rather than steering you into opening an issue.

Under the hood:

Cross-platform parity now has a scanner, a reviewed authority and a baseline, contributed. It inventories the declarations and constants that are supposed to match between the Swift and Kotlin implementations and records the current accepted debt, so that regeneration cannot quietly accept more.
